definition_zh: 战争技术；用于作战的技术体系，涵盖武器、通信、后勤、防护与训练
definition_en: the body of technology developed for, or applied to, the conduct of war
core_image: 实验室的长桌上并排摆着步枪零件、通信电台与作战地图，屏幕的蓝光落在扳手上
scene: 军工展厅里，玻璃柜中并排摆着旧式步枪、通信电台与沙盘，墙上的时间轴把它们连成一条技术演进线。The museum traces warfare technology, the whole technical system of war, from gunpowder to satellite-guided systems.
sceneCN: 这里 warfare technology 指「用于作战的整组技术体系」（第 1 个义项：围绕战争需求发展出的技术集合）；句意为博物馆把战争技术从火药时代一路梳理到卫星制导系统。可辨识物件：玻璃展柜、旧式步枪、通信电台、沙盘、墙上时间轴。

pos.zh: 战争技术；作战技术体系（多作不可数名词，指技术门类时可说 warfare technologies）

forms.label: 通常形式（不可数，指技术门类）
常见同义说法（军事技术）

senses.title: The technical system of war as a whole
senses.definition: the whole set of techniques, devices and systems that a society develops for fighting wars
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会为进行战争而发展出的全部技术、装置与系统
senses.example: The museum traces warfare technology from gunpowder to satellite-guided systems.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把战争技术从火药时代一路梳理到卫星制导系统。
senses.why: warfare names the conduct of war and technology names the systematic handling of an art, so the phrase simply joins the activity to its tools.
senses.whyCN: warfare 指「进行战争」，technology 指「对技艺的系统处理」，短语就是把这项活动与它的工具直接连在一起。

senses.title: Weapons and their platforms
senses.definition: the hardware of war: small arms, artillery, armoured vehicles, aircraft and warships
senses.definitionCN: 战争的硬件部分：轻武器、火炮、装甲车辆、飞机与军舰
senses.example: New alloys moved warfare technology from smoothbore muskets to rifled artillery.
senses.exampleCN: 新的合金材料把战争技术从滑膛枪推进到线膛炮。
senses.why: weapons are the most visible part of the system, so the phrase is often narrowed to the hardware that delivers force.
senses.whyCN: 武器是这套体系中最可见的部分，因此这个短语常被收窄为投送武力的硬件。

senses.title: Command, control, communications and intelligence
senses.titleCN: 指挥、控制、通信与情报技术
senses.definition: the information technology of war: radios, radar, code machines, satellites and data links
senses.definitionCN: 战争的信息技术：电台、雷达、密码机、卫星与数据链
senses.example: Radar and secure radio made warfare technology a matter of information as much as firepower.
senses.exampleCN: 雷达与保密电台使战争技术不仅关乎火力，也关乎信息。
senses.why: once armies could see and speak at a distance, information itself became a weapon, and the phrase absorbed that layer.
senses.whyCN: 当军队能远距离观察与通话，信息本身就成了武器，这个短语也随之吸收了这一层。

senses.title: Logistics and sustainment
senses.definition: the technology that keeps an army supplied, transported, repaired and fed
senses.definitionCN: 维持军队补给、运输、维修与给养的技术
senses.example: Refrigerated depots were as decisive as any warfare technology in the desert campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 在沙漠战役中，冷藏仓库与任何战争技术一样具有决定性。
senses.why: an army that cannot move or eat cannot fight, so supply technology belongs to the same system even though it never fires a shot.
senses.whyCN: 不能移动、不能吃饭的军队无法作战，因此补给技术虽一枪不发，仍属于同一套体系。

senses.title: Training and simulation
senses.definition: the devices and software used to rehearse combat: simulators, ranges and war games
senses.definitionCN: 用于预演作战的器材与软件：模拟器、训练场与兵棋
senses.example: Flight simulators became part of warfare technology only after pilots began learning on the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 只有在飞行员开始在地面学习之后，飞行模拟器才成为战争技术的一部分。
senses.why: rehearsal is part of the conduct of war, so the tools of rehearsal are counted as technology rather than as mere instruction.
senses.whyCN: 预演属于进行战争的一部分，因此预演工具被算作技术，而不只是教学手段。

senses.title: Defensive and protective systems
senses.definition: armour, shelters, camouflage, medical kits and detection systems that limit harm
senses.definitionCN: 装甲、掩体、伪装、医疗装备与探测系统等减少伤害的技术
senses.example: Armour design is a branch of warfare technology that answers the shell.
senses.exampleCN: 装甲设计是回应炮弹的战争技术分支。
senses.why: protection is the mirror image of attack: every new weapon calls out a technology meant to survive it.
senses.whyCN: 防护是进攻的镜像：每一件新武器都会催生一种以求生为目的的技术。

senses.title: Historical phases of military technology
senses.definition: a way of dividing military history into ages such as gunpowder, industrial and information warfare
senses.definitionCN: 把军事史划分为火药时代、工业时代与信息时代等阶段的方式
senses.example: Historians divide warfare technology into gunpowder, industrial and information ages.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把战争技术划分为火药时代、工业时代与信息时代。
senses.why: when a single invention changes how all wars are fought, it becomes a label for an era rather than for one device.
senses.whyCN: 当一项发明改变了所有战争的打法，它就成了一个时代的标签，而不只是一件装置。

senses.title: Borrowed sense: a technical edge in any competition
senses.titleCN: 借喻：任何竞争中的技术优势
senses.definition: by extension, the technical means used to gain advantage in a non-military contest
senses.definitionCN: 引申指在非军事竞争中用来取得优势的技术手段
senses.example: Retailers now study warfare technology to plan their logistics.
senses.exampleCN: 零售商如今研究战争技术来规划自己的物流。
senses.why: the phrase travels well because any hard contest rewards speed, information and supply, which are the three layers named above.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语易于借用，因为任何激烈竞争都奖励速度、信息与补给，而这正是上面点出的三层。

intro.en: Warfare joins two native English words; technology is a Greek compound that reached English through Latin. The phrase itself is a modern English combination. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: warfare 由两个英语本族词合成；technology 是经拉丁语进入英语的希腊复合词。整个短语是近代英语的组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: War came into Middle English from Old North French werre, from a Germanic source usually written *werra 'confusion, strife'; that Germanic form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: war 经古北法语 werre 进入中古英语，源自日耳曼语，通常写作 *werra「混乱、争斗」；这一日耳曼形式属重构。

items.en: Fare is from Old English faran 'to journey, go'. Warfare first meant the going about of war, the conduct of a campaign, not a single battle.
items.cn: fare 来自古英语 faran「行走、前往」。warfare 最初指战争的进行方式、战役的开展，而不是单场战斗。

items.en: Greek tekhnē meant 'art, craft, skill'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes proposed to a root meaning 'to weave or fabricate' is a reconstruction, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: 希腊 tekhnē 意为「技艺、手艺、技能」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它与表示「编织、制作」的词根相连，那只是重构，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Greek logos meant 'word, account, reason'; the combining form -logia named a systematic study, and Latin technologia passed this pattern to English technology.
items.cn: 希腊 logos 意为「言说、叙述、理性」；组合形式 -logia 指系统的学问，拉丁 technologia 把这一构词模式传给英语 technology。

items.en: Technology entered English in the seventeenth century; warfare technology as a fixed two-word label belongs to modern military writing, and its exact first printed use is not recorded.
items.cn: technology 在十七世纪进入英语；warfare technology 作为固定双词标签属于现代军事写作，其最早印刷记录不明。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation and root shapes): no dictionary fixes the first use of the full phrase; the Germanic source of war and the Greek root of tekhnē are reconstructions, so competing forms are alternatives, not proven variants.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根形态）：没有辞书确定这一完整短语的首次使用；war 的日耳曼来源与 tekhnē 的希腊词根均属重构，因此其他写法只是备选，并非已证实的变体。

note.en: Group one holds expressions built from the same war or technology words and easily confused; group two holds neighbouring ideas about the means of fighting.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 war 或 technology 词干、容易混淆的说法；第二组是有关作战手段的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The standard term for technology used by armed forces; warfare technology stresses the activity of war rather than the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指武装部队使用的技术的标准说法；warfare technology 更强调战争这一活动，而不是军队机构。

entries.definition: The conduct of war itself. It names the activity, while warfare technology names one class of means used in that activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指战争行为本身；它说的是活动，而 warfare technology 说的是这一活动中所用的一类手段。

entries.definition: Collectively the weapons; it leaves communications, logistics and training outside the frame.
entries.definitionCN: 统称武器；把通信、后勤与训练留在框架之外。

entries.definition: Technology as used at the front; the longer phrase warfare technology also covers factories, depots and classrooms behind the line.
entries.definitionCN: 指前线使用的技术；warfare technology 还涵盖战线后方的工厂、仓库与课堂。

entries.definition: The principles by which a force plans to fight; doctrine is thought, whereas the phrase in question is hardware and technique.
entries.definitionCN: 指部队计划作战的原则；doctrine 是思想，而本短语指硬件与技术。

entries.definition: The protective side of the field; it excludes offensive weapons and power projection.
entries.definitionCN: 指这一领域中的防护一侧，不含进攻性武器与力量投送。

entries.definition: A rivalry in which rivals build more or better weapons; it is a pattern of behaviour, not a body of knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 指对手不断扩充或改良武器的竞争；它是一种行为模式，不是知识门类。

entries.definition: The branch that builds bridges, roads, fortifications and obstacles; it is a part of warfare technology, not its whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指修筑桥梁、道路、工事与障碍物的分支；它是战争技术的一部分，而非全部。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real English words, the Greek roots of technology and the layers named above.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的英语词、technology 的希腊词根，以及各义项中点出的层次。

normal.en: war + fare: fare means 'to go', so warfare is the going about of war.
normal.cn: war + fare：fare 意为「行走」，因此 warfare 就是「打仗这回事怎么走」。

normal.en: technology is tekhnē 'craft' plus -logia 'study': the study of crafts, then the crafts themselves.
normal.cn: technology 是 tekhnē「技艺」加 -logia「学问」：先指对技艺的研究，后指技艺本身。

normal.en: Three layers to remember: weapons, information, supply.
normal.cn: 记住三个层次：武器、信息、补给。

normal.en: Every weapon calls out a defence: shell and armour grow together.
normal.cn: 每件武器都催生一种防护：炮弹与装甲一同成长。

normal.en: The family runs war, warfare, technology, technical, technique, technologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 war、warfare、technology、technical、technique、technologist。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox that keeps growing faster than the hands that use it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只工具箱，它增长的速度快过使用它的双手。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose ticks are inventions, each tick changing how the next war runs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，指针的每一下都是一项发明，每一下都改变下一场战争的走法。

abstract.en: Picture a contest judged not by strength alone but by who sees and supplies faster.
abstract.cn: 想象一场较量，胜负不只取决于力量，还取决于谁看得更快、供得更快。

examples.en: The exhibition shows how warfare technology changed the shape of fortifications.
examples.cn: 展览展示了战争技术如何改变防御工事的形态。

examples.en: Scholars debate whether warfare technology drives strategy or follows it.
examples.cn: 学者们争论战争技术是驱动战略，还是跟随战略。

examples.en: Civilian firms now sell components that end up in warfare technology.
examples.cn: 民用公司如今出售最终进入战争技术的零部件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「war（战争）+ fare（走）」——跟着战争走的那一整套器具与手艺 → 战争技术

root: war 经古北法语 werre 源自日耳曼语 *werra「混乱、争斗」；fare 来自古英语 faran「行走」，warfare 原指战争的进行。technology 来自希腊 tekhnē「技艺」+ logos「学问」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings spread outward from one image: a toolbox built for war, then narrowed to weapons, widened to information and supply, extended to rehearsal and protection, dated as eras, and finally borrowed by any hard contest.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个意象向外展开：为战争打造的工具箱，先收窄到武器，再扩到信息与补给，延伸到预演与防护，被当作时代来分期，最后被任何激烈竞争借用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a workbench where a rifle, a radio and a supply map lie side by side under one lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张工作台上，步枪、电台与补给地图并排放在同一盏灯下。

branches.en: THE HARDWARE CORE: the phrase begins with the arms that deliver force.
branches.cn: 硬件核心：这个短语从投送武力的武器开始。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE HALF: seeing, speaking and feeding decide whether the hardware can act.
branches.cn: 看不见的一半：看见、通话与供养决定硬件能否行动。

branches.en: LEARNING AND SURVIVING: rehearsal prepares the hand, protection keeps it alive.
branches.cn: 学会与活下来：预演训练双手，防护让双手活着。

branches.en: TIME LAYER: one decisive invention turns the field into a named age.
branches.cn: 时间层：一项决定性发明把这一领域变成一个被命名的时代。

branches.en: BORROWED EDGE: any contest that rewards speed and supply can use the name.
branches.cn: 借来的优势：任何奖励速度与补给的竞争都能借用这个名字。

intro.en: The phrase has two English words and one Greek-derived technical word, so every piece can be read on its own.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个英语词与一个希腊来源的技术词构成，因此每一块都能单独读出。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved here: war is Germanic, fare is Old English and technology is Greek. The Latin role was only to pass technologia on to English, so no Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词根：war 属日耳曼语，fare 属古英语，technology 属希腊语。拉丁语的作用只是把 technologia 传给英语，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.structure: war (Old North French werre, from Germanic *werra, strife)
items.meaningCN: 群体间有组织的武装冲突
items.example: The country had known war for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家已经经历了十年战争。

items.structure: fare (Old English faran, to journey, go)
items.meaning: to go along, hence a course of action
items.meaningCN: 行走，引申为行事的过程
items.example: Sailors fared across the narrow sea.
items.exampleCN: 水手们穿过狭窄的海面。

items.example: Guerrilla warfare avoids open battles.
items.exampleCN: 游击战避免正面会战。

items.meaning: systematic knowledge applied to practical arts
items.meaningCN: 应用于实用技艺的系统知识
items.example: Technology changed how the depot was run.
items.exampleCN: 技术改变了仓库的运作方式。

items.meaning: relating to a craft or its details
items.meaningCN: 与技艺或其细节有关的
items.example: The failure was technical, not strategic.
items.exampleCN: 这次失败是技术性的，而非战略性的。

items.meaning: a particular way of doing a skilled task
items.meaningCN: 完成熟练任务的特定方法
items.example: The crew practised a new loading technique.
items.exampleCN: 机组练习了一种新的装载方法。

items.example: Technological change outpaced the rules.
items.exampleCN: 技术变化快过了规则。

items.example: A technologist tested the new radio.
items.exampleCN: 一位技术专家测试了新电台。

items.meaning: the standard synonym for the field
items.meaningCN: 这一领域的标准同义说法
items.example: Military technology includes field hospitals.
items.exampleCN: 军事技术包括野战医院。

definition_zh: 停战；休战协定；（特定语境）停战纪念日
definition_en: an agreement between opposing forces to stop fighting for a period, or the suspension of hostilities itself
core_image: 阵地中央插着一面白旗，两支枪口朝下，怀表停在双方约定的时刻
scene: 战壕两侧的士兵把步枪靠在胸墙上，中间的空地被插上一面白旗，双方军官在泥地里交换签字的纸张。The two commanders signed an armistice, a formal written halt of the guns, before dawn, and the firing stopped along the line.
sceneCN: 这里 armistice 指「交战双方停止战斗的正式约定」（第 1 个义项：以文书确认的休战安排）；句意为两位指挥官在黎明前签署停战协定，整条战线随即沉寂。可辨识物件：胸墙、步枪、白旗、签字纸张、怀表。

pos.zh: 停战；休战协定；停战期（可数，复数 armistices）

senses.title: A formal agreement to stop fighting
senses.definition: a formal agreement between two opposing forces to suspend fighting, usually while a peace is negotiated
senses.definitionCN: 交战双方暂停战斗的正式约定，通常用于谈判和平期间
senses.example: The two commanders signed an armistice before dawn, and the guns fell silent along the line.
senses.exampleCN: 两位指挥官在黎明前签署停战协定，整条战线随即沉寂。
senses.why: arma 'arms' plus sistere 'to make stand still' gives the literal picture: weapons are made to stand and stop.
senses.whyCN: arma「武器」加 sistere「使立定不动」给出了字面图景：让武器站住、停下。

senses.title: The act of concluding such an agreement
senses.definition: the diplomatic act of negotiating and concluding a suspension of hostilities
senses.definitionCN: 谈判并缔结休战安排的外交行为
senses.example: Delegates argued for weeks before the armistice was signed.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们争论了数周，停战协定才得以签署。
senses.why: the noun can name the event as well as the paper, as with many legal acts in English.
senses.whyCN: 和英语中许多法律行为一样，这个名词既可指文书，也可指事件本身。

senses.title: The period of suspended hostilities
senses.definition: the interval during which the agreement is in force and no fighting takes place
senses.definitionCN: 协定生效、战斗停止的这段时间
senses.example: During the armistice, engineers repaired the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 停战期间，工程人员修复了那座桥。
senses.why: once signed, the agreement fills a stretch of time, and the word shifts from document to duration.
senses.whyCN: 签署之后，协定占据一段时间，词义便从文书转到时段。

senses.title: A local or tactical suspension
senses.definition: a limited halt arranged by local commanders for rescue, burial or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 由当地指挥官为救援、掩埋或谈判安排的有限停火
senses.example: A local armistice let medics recover the wounded.
senses.exampleCN: 一项局部停战让医护得以抬回伤员。
senses.why: the same instrument works at any scale, so a colonel can sign one without ending a war.
senses.whyCN: 同一工具可用于任何规模，因此一名上校也能签署停战而不结束战争。

senses.title: A legally binding instrument
senses.definition: the written terms that fix a line, a timetable and the duties of both sides
senses.definitionCN: 规定分界线、时间表与双方义务的书面条款
senses.example: The armistice set the line of control in legally binding terms.
senses.exampleCN: 停战协定以具有法律约束力的条款确定了控制线。
senses.why: armistice terms often serve as the legal skeleton for a later peace, so the word carries treaty-like weight.
senses.whyCN: 停战条款常成为日后和平的法律骨架，因此这个词带有条约般的分量。

senses.title: The commemorative name Armistice Day
senses.definition: the name given in several countries to the anniversary of the 1918 armistice
senses.definitionCN: 若干国家给一九一八年停战周年所起的名称
senses.example: In several countries Armistice Day marks the eleventh hour of the eleventh day.
senses.exampleCN: 在若干国家，停战纪念日纪念的是十一月十一日的第十一个小时。
senses.why: a single historical armistice became a proper name, so the common noun turned into a calendar label.
senses.whyCN: 一次历史性的停战变成了专名，于是普通名词转为日历标签。

senses.title: A figurative pause in a quarrel
senses.definition: by extension, a temporary halt in any hostile contest, such as a feud or a campaign
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何敌对较量中的暂时中止，如世仇或攻势
senses.example: The rivals reached an armistice in their advertising war.
senses.exampleCN: 对手在广告战中达成了停战。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the military shape: two sides, a line, and a pause that is not yet peace.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留了军事形态：两方、一条线，以及一个还不是和平的暂停。

senses.title: Abstraction: an agreed pause in a hostile relation
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：敌对关系中的约定暂停
senses.definition: any agreed suspension of a hostile relationship, understood as a pause rather than a resolution
senses.definitionCN: 任何敌对关系的约定性中止，理解为暂停而非解决
senses.example: An armistice is not peace; it only stops the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 停战不是和平；它只是让钟停住。
senses.why: the word's deepest sense is procedural: it halts action without settling the dispute, which is why it fits so many conflicts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最深的一层是程序性的：它停止行动，却不解决争端，因此适用于许多冲突。

intro.en: Armistice reached English through French from a medieval Latin compound joining arma 'arms' to sistere 'to stand still'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: armistice 经法语进入英语，来自中世纪拉丁语复合词，把 arma「武器」与 sistere「站住」连接起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arma, a plural noun, meant 'arms, weapons, equipment'; the related verb armare meant 'to equip for war'.
items.cn: arma 是复数名词，意为「武器、装备」；相关动词 armare 意为「为战争装备」。

items.en: Sistere meant 'to cause to stand, to stop, to halt'; it is related to stare 'to stand', and the suffix -stitium named a stopping.
items.cn: sistere 意为「使站立、使停止、使停下」；它与 stare「站立」相关，后缀 -stitium 表示「停止」。

items.en: Medieval Latin armistitium combined the two ideas as 'a standing still of arms', the literal ancestor of the modern word.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 armistitium 把两个概念合成「武器的静止」，是现代词的字面前身。

items.en: The French form armistice spread in the seventeenth century and entered English soon after; early uses concerned temporary suspensions in European wars.
items.cn: 法语形式 armistice 在十七世纪流行，随后进入英语；早期用法指欧洲战争中的暂时休战。

items.en: After the armistice of 11 November 1918, the date was observed as Armistice Day in several countries; some later renamed it for all war dead.
items.cn: 一九一八年十一月十一日停战之后，若干国家把这一天作为停战日纪念；有些国家后来改名以纪念所有战争死者。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English citation and suffix analysis): dictionaries do not fix the earliest English use, and the division of -stitium between sistere and statio is an interpretation rather than a recorded fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与后缀分析）：辞书未确定最早的英语用例；把 -stitium 归于 sistere 还是 statio 只是一种解释，并非有记录的事实。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the arms or standing-still stock, easily confused with armistice; group two holds the neighbouring stop-fighting terms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「武器」或「立定」词干、易与 armistice 混淆的词；第二组是邻近的「停止战斗」类词。

entries.definition: Military equipment and the process of building it up; it shares arma with armistice but means arming, not disarming.
entries.definitionCN: 指军事装备及扩充军备的过程；与 armistice 同出 arma，但意思是「武装」而非「停止武装」。

entries.definition: Protective covering for the body or a vehicle; it comes through Old French from Latin armatura, a derivative of armare.
entries.definitionCN: 指护身或护车的装甲；经古法语来自拉丁 armatura，是 armare 的派生词。

entries.definition: A stop in fighting agreed for a short time; it is the everyday older synonym and often implies a shorter pause than armistice.
entries.definitionCN: 指短时间约定的停火；这是更早的日常同义词，通常暗示比 armistice 更短的暂停。

entries.definition: The boundary fixed by an armistice; the phrase names a place, while armistice names the agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 指停战协定确定的界线；该短语指地点，而 armistice 指协定。

entries.definition: An order or agreement to stop firing; it can be local or informal, whereas armistice usually implies a formal instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 指停止射击的命令或约定，可局部、可非正式；armistice 通常暗示正式文书。

entries.definition: A binding agreement between states; a peace treaty settles the war, while an armistice only suspends it.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家间有约束力的协定；和平条约解决战争，而停战只把战争暂停。

entries.definition: The formal surrender of a force on stated terms; it is one-sided, unlike an armistice between equals.
entries.definitionCN: 指一支部队按条件正式投降；它是单方面的，不同于对等双方的停战。

entries.definition: A return from combat readiness to normal duty; it is an internal order, not a bargain between enemies.
entries.definitionCN: 指从战备状态回到正常值勤；这是内部命令，不是敌我之间的交易。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the historical date and the real compounds built on the same stem.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、那个历史日期，以及同词干构成的真实复合词。

normal.en: arma 'arms' + sistere 'stand still': arms made to stand still.
normal.cn: arma「武器」+ sistere「站住」：让武器站住不动。

normal.en: The medieval form armistitium is the same picture written out: a stopping of arms.
normal.cn: 中世纪形式 armistitium 把这个图景写全：武器的停止。

normal.en: The eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month is the 1918 armistice.
normal.cn: 十一月十一日第十一个小时，就是一九一八年的停战时刻。

normal.en: The family runs arms, armament, disarm, disarmament, armoury.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arms、armament、disarm、disarmament、armoury。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with armour: one stops the guns, the other stops the bullet.
normal.cn: 不要与 armour 混淆：一个让枪停下，一个让子弹停下。

abstract.en: Picture two boxers touching gloves: the fight pauses, but the match is not decided.
abstract.cn: 想象两名拳手碰拳：打斗暂停了，但比赛尚未分出胜负。

abstract.en: Picture a clock stopped by agreement rather than by damage.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟是被约定停住的，而不是被损坏停住的。

abstract.en: Picture a door held ajar between two rooms: neither closed nor open.
abstract.cn: 想象两个房间之间一扇半开的门：既没关上，也没敞开。

examples.en: The armistice left the city divided along a temporary line.
examples.cn: 停战协定沿一条临时界线把城市分开。

examples.en: Neither side trusted the armistice to last through the winter.
examples.cn: 双方都不相信停战能维持整个冬天。

examples.en: A signed armistice bought time for the peace conference.
examples.cn: 签署停战协定为和平会议争取了时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「arm（武器）+ st（停住）+ ice（冰）」——武器冻住不动 → 停战

root: 拉丁 arma「武器」+ sistere「使站住」，中世纪拉丁 armistitium 字面为「武器的静止」。sistere 与 stare「站立」相关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one act: weapons are made to stand still. The act becomes a signed document, then a stretch of time, then a local arrangement, then a legal instrument, then a calendar name, then a metaphor for any quarrel and finally a general name for a pause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个动作展开：让武器立定。这个动作先成为签署的文书，再成为一段时间，再成为局部安排，再成为法律工具，再成为日历名称，再成为任何争执的比喻，最后成为「暂停」的通称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rifles stacked upright with a white flag between them, a watch stopped at the agreed hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：步枪竖着架起，中间一面白旗，怀表停在约定的时刻。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: words on paper make the weapons stand still and bind both sides.
branches.cn: 文书：纸上的文字让武器立定，并约束双方。

branches.en: THE EVENT AND ITS DURATION: signing opens a stretch of quiet.
branches.cn: 事件与时长：签署打开一段安静。

branches.en: THE DATE: one armistice becomes a name on the calendar.
branches.cn: 日期：一次停战变成日历上的名称。

branches.en: THE SMALL SCALE: the same act shrinks to a colonel's local bargain.
branches.cn: 小尺度：同一动作可缩小为上校的局部交易。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any feud can borrow the white flag, because a pause is not a settlement.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何争执都能借这面白旗，因为暂停并不等于解决。

intro.en: Armistice is a Latin compound whose two halves still build other English words, so it can be read as prefix-like element plus root.
intro.cn: armistice 是拉丁复合词，两个部分仍构成其他英语词，因此可按「前成分加词根」读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin arma gives arm, armament, disarm and armoury; Latin sistere gives insist, resist, persist and assist, all through the sense of standing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 arma 衍生 arm、armament、disarm 与 armoury；拉丁 sistere 经「站立」之义衍生 insist、resist、persist 与 assist。

items.example: The legion laid down its arma.
items.exampleCN: 军团放下了武器。

items.structure: sistere (Latin verb, to cause to stand)
items.example: The guard was ordered to sistere.
items.exampleCN: 守卫奉命站定。

items.example: The armistice held for six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 停战维持了六周。

items.meaning: equipment for war; the act of arming
items.example: Naval armament expanded before the war.
items.exampleCN: 战前海军军备扩张。

items.example: The patrol was disarmed at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 巡逻队在门口被解除武装。

items.example: Disarmament talks resumed in spring.
items.exampleCN: 裁军谈判在春季恢复。

items.meaning: a place where weapons are stored
items.example: The armoury kept the reserve rifles.
items.exampleCN: 军械库保管备用步枪。

items.example: She insisted on a written term.
items.exampleCN: 她坚持要有一项书面条款。

items.example: The unit resisted for a week.
items.exampleCN: 该部队抵抗了一周。

items.example: Both generals initialled the armistice agreement.
items.exampleCN: 两位将军草签了停战协议。

definition_zh: 停火；停火命令或协议；停火状态；引申指激烈攻击的暂停
definition_en: an order or agreement to stop shooting, the state of not shooting, or a temporary halt of intense attacks
core_image: 阵地上密集的曳光弹突然消失，枪管仍在冒烟，士兵从掩体后探出头
scene: 清晨的街区里，广播喇叭传出一段命令，交火双方的枪声先后停下，居民从地下室慢慢走出来。The mediator announced a ceasefire, an order to stop shooting, and the guns fell silent by noon.
sceneCN: 这里 ceasefire 指「双方停止射击的命令或安排」（第 1 个义项：使火力停止的约定）；句意为调解人宣布停火，到中午枪声就停了。可辨识物件：广播喇叭、掩体、步枪、地下室出口、停下的弹壳。

pos.zh: 停火；停火命令或协议；停火状态（可数，复数 ceasefires）

senses.title: An order or agreement to stop shooting
senses.titleCN: 停止射击的命令或约定
senses.definition: an instruction or arrangement by which opposing forces stop firing, usually for a set time or area
senses.definitionCN: 交战双方停止射击的指令或安排，通常限定时间或区域
senses.example: The mediator announced a ceasefire, and the shooting stopped by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 调解人宣布停火，到中午枪声就停了。
senses.why: cease is 'to stop' and fire is 'shooting', so the compound names the stopping of shooting directly.
senses.whyCN: cease 是「停止」，fire 是「射击」，因此这个复合词直接命名「停止射击」。

senses.title: The state of no firing
senses.definition: the condition in which no shots are being fired along a line or in an area
senses.definitionCN: 沿某条战线或某个区域内没有射击的状态
senses.example: A fragile ceasefire held while the negotiators met.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判代表会面期间，一个脆弱的停火得以维持。
senses.why: a command creates a state, and English often lets the same noun name both the order and the condition it produces.
senses.whyCN: 命令造成状态，英语常让同一个名词既指命令，也指它造成的状态。

senses.title: A written or spoken agreement
senses.titleCN: 书面或口头的停火协议
senses.definition: a formal or informal deal that fixes when and where firing will stop
senses.definitionCN: 确定何时何地停止射击的正式或非正式约定
senses.example: The ceasefire agreement set a corridor for aid.
senses.exampleCN: 停火协议划出了一条援助走廊。
senses.why: the word is used for the document as well as the act, as with treaty and armistice.
senses.whyCN: 和 treaty、armistice 一样，这个词既指行为，也指文书。

senses.title: A unilateral declaration
senses.definition: a halt declared by one side without the other's consent, often to gain political advantage
senses.definitionCN: 一方未经对方同意而宣布的停止射击，常为取得政治优势
senses.example: The government offered a unilateral ceasefire at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 政府在午夜单方面提出停火。
senses.why: one party can stop shooting alone; the word does not require reciprocity, though it often implies it.
senses.whyCN: 一方可以独自停止射击；这个词并不要求对等，尽管通常暗示对等。

senses.title: A humanitarian pause
senses.definition: a short, local halt arranged so that aid, evacuation or burial can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 为援助、撤离或掩埋而安排的短时局部停火
senses.example: A humanitarian ceasefire let convoys cross the front.
senses.exampleCN: 人道主义停火让车队穿过前线。
senses.why: when the purpose is saving lives rather than settling the war, the compound takes a humanitarian modifier.
senses.whyCN: 当目的在救命而非解决战争时，这个复合词会带人道主义修饰语。

senses.title: A ceasefire that is broken
senses.definition: a halt that fails, with firing resuming and blame traded by both sides
senses.definitionCN: 未能维持、射击恢复且双方互相指责的停火
senses.example: The ceasefire collapsed after a single mortar round.
senses.exampleCN: 一发迫击炮弹就让停火崩溃。
senses.why: a pause is fragile because it rests on restraint, not on settlement; the word therefore appears with collapse and violation.
senses.whyCN: 暂停是脆弱的，因为它依赖克制而非解决；因此这个词常与「崩溃」「违反」搭配。

senses.title: Figurative halt of intense attacks
senses.definition: by extension, a pause in a fierce non-military campaign such as cyber attacks or hostile publicity
senses.definitionCN: 引申指网络攻击或敌意宣传等非军事激烈行动的暂停
senses.example: The platforms called a ceasefire in the disinformation war.
senses.exampleCN: 各平台在虚假信息战中呼吁停火。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the gunfire image and applies it to any exchange of blows at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留枪火意象，把它用于任何远程交火。

senses.title: Abstraction: a cooling of a conflict system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：冲突系统的冷却
senses.definition: any agreed reduction of intensity in a hostile system, seen as a cooling rather than a cure
senses.definitionCN: 敌对系统中任何约定的强度下降，被视为降温而非治愈
senses.example: A ceasefire lowers the temperature, but the dispute remains.
senses.exampleCN: 停火降低了温度，但争端仍在。
senses.why: the deepest sense is thermodynamic rather than legal: intensity falls, structure stays.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是热力学式的而非法律式的：强度下降，结构不变。

intro.en: Ceasefire joins an Old French verb of stopping to the native English word for fire. The compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceasefire 把古法语「停止」动词与英语本族词「火」连接起来，属近代复合词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old French cesser 'to stop, give way' came from Latin cessare, a frequentative of cedere 'to go, yield'.
items.cn: 古法语 cesser「停止、让出」来自拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「行走、让出」的反复动词。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, withdraw, yield'; cessare repeated the action, giving the sense of holding off or stopping.
items.cn: cedere 意为「行走、退去、让出」；cessare 表示反复，产生「退开、停止」之义。

items.en: Fire descends from Old English fȳr and Proto-Germanic *fōr; the Indo-European ancestor is usually reconstructed as *perjos, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: fire 承自英语 fȳr 与原始日耳曼语 *fōr；其印欧祖形通常重构为 *perjos，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: The compound cease-fire appeared in military writing in the early twentieth century, when industrialized armies needed a word for a scheduled halt of artillery.
items.cn: cease-fire 这一复合词在二十世纪初的军事写作中出现，当时工业化军队需要一个词来指按计划停止炮击。

items.en: After the First World War the term moved into diplomacy and then into figurative use for any intense campaign.
items.cn: 第一次世界大战之后，这个词进入外交领域，随后引申用于任何激烈行动。

items.en: Source uncertain (coinage date): dictionaries differ on the first printed use, and the Indo-European roots of both fire and cedere are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（造词年代）：辞书对最早印刷用例说法不一，且 fire 与 cedere 的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds stop-fighting terms that overlap with ceasefire; group two holds the wider diplomatic and military ideas around it.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ceasefire 重叠的停止战斗类词；第二组是围绕它的更广的外交与军事概念。

entries.definition: Simply to stop or bring to an end; it needs an object, as in cease firing, and carries no agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指停止或终止；需要宾语，如停止射击，且不含约定之意。

entries.definition: The act of stopping, often used in phrases such as cessation of hostilities; it is more formal and less specific than ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指停止的行为，常用于「停止敌对行动」等短语；比 ceasefire 更正式、更宽泛。

entries.definition: Agreements limiting weapons types or numbers; they shape the future of a conflict rather than stop present firing.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制武器种类或数量的协定；它塑造冲突的未来，而非停止当下的射击。

entries.definition: A short agreed stop in fighting; it is older and plainer, and often briefer than a ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指约定短时停止战斗；更古老、更口语，通常比停火更短暂。

entries.definition: A formal suspension of hostilities, usually while peace is negotiated; it is generally more binding than a ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式休战，通常在谈判和平期间；一般比停火更具约束力。

entries.definition: A settlement that ends a war and fixes the postwar order; a ceasefire only stops the shooting.
entries.definitionCN: 指结束战争、确定战后秩序的解决方案；停火只停止射击。

entries.definition: A deliberate lowering of tension or force; it may occur without any formal halt in firing.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意降低紧张或武力强度；不一定伴随正式停火。

entries.definition: An area where fighting is excluded by agreement; it is a spatial arrangement that a ceasefire may protect.
entries.definitionCN: 指经约定排除战斗的区域；这是空间安排，停火可用于保护它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real words, the Latin chain behind cease and the compound's modern military setting.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实词、cease 背后的拉丁链条，以及这个复合词的近代军事背景。

normal.en: cease 'stop' + fire 'shooting': the name says exactly what stops.
normal.cn: cease「停止」+ fire「射击」：这个名字直接说出停的是什么。

normal.en: Cease goes back through French to Latin cessare, a repeated cedere, 'to withdraw'.
normal.cn: cease 经法语上溯拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「退去」的反复形式。

normal.en: The family runs cease, cessation, ceasefire, fire, gunfire, firepower.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cease、cessation、ceasefire、fire、gunfire、firepower。

normal.en: A ceasefire is a pause, not a settlement: the war is still legally alive.
normal.cn: 停火是暂停而非解决：战争在法律上仍然存在。

normal.en: Typical partners are declare, broker, violate and collapse.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「宣布」「斡旋」「违反」「崩溃」。

abstract.en: Picture a loud machine switched to silent mode without being unplugged.
abstract.cn: 想象一台吵闹的机器被调到静音，却并未拔掉电源。

abstract.en: Picture a fever brought down by medicine: the disease is still in the body.
abstract.cn: 想象用药物把高烧退下：病还在体内。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifted in a game: play stops, but the score is unchanged.
abstract.cn: 想象比赛中举起一只手：比赛停了，比分未变。

examples.en: Both sides accused each other of breaking the ceasefire.
examples.cn: 双方都指责对方破坏停火。

examples.en: The ceasefire allowed aid trucks to reach the valley.
examples.cn: 停火让援助卡车得以抵达山谷。

examples.en: A ceasefire without monitoring rarely lasts.
examples.cn: 没有监督的停火很少能持久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cease（停止）+ fire（开火）」——停止开火 → 停火

root: cease 经古法语 cesser 来自拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「退去、让出」的反复动词；fire 来自古英语 fȳr，属日耳曼语本族词。复合为「停止射击」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from the literal order to stop shooting, through the state and the document, to unilateral and humanitarian versions, to a broken halt, a metaphor for any campaign and finally a general cooling of conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面的停止射击命令出发，经过停火状态与文书，再到单方面与人道主义变体，再到被破坏的停火，再到任何行动的比喻，最后落到冲突的普遍降温。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of rifles lowered at once while smoke still rises from the barrels.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排步枪同时放下，枪管仍在冒烟。

branches.en: ORDER AND CONDITION: the command creates the quiet it names.
branches.cn: 命令与状态：命令造出它所命名的安静。

branches.en: PAPER OR ONE VOICE: a deal can be signed by two or offered by one.
branches.cn: 纸面或单方：协议可由两方签署，也可由一方提出。

branches.en: MERCY AND FAILURE: a pause to save lives can still break under one shell.
branches.cn: 仁慈与失败：为救命的暂停仍可能被一发炮弹打破。

branches.en: BORROWED GUNFIRE: any distant exchange of blows can be paused this way.
branches.cn: 借来的枪火：任何远程交火都能这样暂停。

branches.en: COOLING, NOT CURE: intensity falls while the structure of the dispute remains.
branches.cn: 降温而非治愈：强度下降，争端结构仍在。

intro.en: Ceasefire is a transparent English compound of a Latin-derived verb and a native noun, so both halves are readable.
intro.cn: ceasefire 是透明的英语复合词，由拉丁来源动词与本族名词构成，两部分都可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin cessare and cedere build cease, cessation, cession and concede; fire has no Latin root and is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cessare 与 cedere 构成 cease、cessation、cession 与 concede；fire 无拉丁词根，属日耳曼语。

items.structure: cease (Old French cesser, from Latin cessare)
items.meaning: to stop, bring to an end
items.example: The battery ceased firing at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 炮组在黄昏停止射击。

items.example: The Latin verb implied repeated yielding.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词含反复退让之意。

items.example: The root also underlies concede and cession.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也构成 concede 与 cession。

items.example: Cessation of hostilities was announced.
items.exampleCN: 宣布停止敌对行动。

items.example: The fire from the ridge pinned the patrol.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上的火力压制了巡逻队。

items.meaning: the volume of fire a force can deliver
items.meaningCN: 一支部队能投送的火力
items.example: Their firepower forced a retreat.
items.exampleCN: 他们的火力迫使对方撤退。

items.example: Gunfire echoed across the square.
items.exampleCN: 枪声在广场上回荡。

items.example: The ceasefire agreement named two monitors.
items.exampleCN: 停火协议指定了两名监督员。

items.meaning: the same term in older style
items.example: Older reports wrote cease-fire.
items.exampleCN: 较早的报道写作 cease-fire。

definition_zh: 和平条约；结束战争并安排战后关系的正式协定
definition_en: a formal agreement between states that ends a war and settles the terms of peace
core_image: 长桌上摊开一叠厚纸文件，两支笔搁在签名处，窗外礼炮的烟还未散
scene: 古老议事厅的长桌上摊开一叠文件，战胜国与战败国的代表依次在末页签名，随后窗外响起礼炮。The peace treaty, the formal settlement that ends a war, redrew the border and ended four years of fighting.
sceneCN: 这里 peace treaty 指「结束战争并安排战后关系的正式协定」（第 1 个义项：以条约形式确认的和平安排）；句意为这份和平条约重划了边界，结束了四年战事。可辨识物件：长桌、厚文件、签名笔、代表席位、窗外礼炮的烟。

pos.zh: 和平条约；和约（可数，复数 peace treaties）

senses.title: A formal agreement ending a war
senses.definition: a binding agreement by which warring states end hostilities and establish peace
senses.definitionCN: 交战国结束敌对、建立和平的有约束力协定
senses.example: The peace treaty redrew the border and ended four years of fighting.
senses.exampleCN: 这份和平条约重划了边界，结束了四年战事。
senses.why: peace names the settled state and treaty names the instrument, so the phrase is the paper that produces the state.
senses.whyCN: peace 指安定的状态，treaty 指工具，因此短语就是「制造这一状态的那份文书」。

senses.title: The document itself
senses.definition: the physical or archived text containing the agreed clauses and signatures
senses.definitionCN: 载有议定条款与签名的实物或存档文本
senses.example: The peace treaty is kept in a sealed vault.
senses.exampleCN: 这份和平条约保存在密封的库房里。
senses.why: an agreement needs a body, and English names the body with the same words as the agreement.
senses.whyCN: 协定需要一个载体，英语用同一个说法既指协定，也指载体。

senses.title: The signing act and ceremony
senses.definition: the ceremony at which authorized representatives sign and seal the agreement
senses.definitionCN: 授权代表签署并盖章的仪式
senses.example: Cameras recorded the peace treaty being signed at Versailles.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影机记录下在凡尔赛签署和平条约的场景。
senses.why: the phrase can name an event, especially when the ceremony is historically important.
senses.whyCN: 当仪式具有历史重要性时，这个短语也可指事件。

senses.title: The substantive clauses
senses.definition: the terms on territory, reparations, disarmament, frontiers and responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 有关领土、赔款、裁军、边界与责任的条款
senses.example: The peace treaty imposed reparations and a reduced army.
senses.exampleCN: 和约规定了赔款并限制了军队规模。
senses.why: what makes a treaty consequential is its clauses, so the phrase is often used for the terms rather than the ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 条约的分量来自条款，因此这个短语常指条款而非仪式。

senses.title: A postwar settlement framework
senses.definition: the whole set of arrangements that a settlement creates for the defeated and victorious states
senses.definitionCN: 一次解决方案为战败国与战胜国建立的整体安排
senses.example: The peace treaty shaped European politics for a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这份和约塑造了一代人的欧洲政治。
senses.why: a treaty does not only stop fighting; it builds an order, and the phrase carries that order with it.
senses.whyCN: 条约不只停止战斗，还建立秩序，这个短语也带着那套秩序。

senses.title: A type: bilateral or multilateral
senses.definition: one of the recognized kinds of settlement, signed by two states or by many
senses.definitionCN: 公认的解决方案类型之一，由两国或多国签署
senses.example: The bilateral peace treaty avoided a wider conference.
senses.exampleCN: 双边和平条约避免了更大范围的会议。
senses.why: diplomats classify settlements by the number of signatories, and the phrase takes those labels.
senses.whyCN: 外交官按签署方数量给解决方案分类，这个短语也随之带上这些标签。

senses.title: Figurative formal reconciliation
senses.definition: by extension, a formal settlement of a long non-military quarrel between institutions or persons
senses.definitionCN: 引申指机构或个人之间长期非军事争执的正式解决
senses.example: The two firms signed a peace treaty over the patent dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司就专利争端签署了「和平条约」。
senses.why: the metaphor works because a long feud, like a war, needs a public instrument to end it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为长期争执和战争一样，需要一份公开文书来结束。

senses.title: Abstraction: a framework for repairing a relationship
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：修复关系的框架
senses.definition: any agreed set of terms by which former adversaries rebuild a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 昔日对手重建关系的任何议定条款集合
senses.example: A peace treaty is the architecture of trust, not trust itself.
senses.exampleCN: 和平条约是信任的建筑，而不是信任本身。
senses.why: the deepest sense is structural: the document supplies a frame that feelings may later fill.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是结构性的：文书提供框架，情感日后才填入。

intro.en: Peace comes from Latin pax through Old French; treaty comes from Latin tractatus, a handling or negotiation. The phrase is an English diplomatic collocation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: peace 经古法语来自拉丁 pax；treaty 来自拉丁 tractatus「处理、商谈」。短语是英语外交搭配。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pax (genitive pacis) meant 'peace, compact, agreement'; it also gave pact and pacify.
items.cn: pax（属格 pacis）意为「和平、约定、协议」；也衍生 pact 与 pacify。

items.en: Old French pais or pees carried the word into English as peace in the twelfth century.
items.cn: 古法语 pais 或 pees 在十二世纪把这个词带入英语，成为 peace。

items.en: Tractatus meant 'a handling, discussion, treatise', from tractare 'to handle, manage, negotiate', a frequentative of trahere 'to draw'.
items.cn: tractatus 意为「处理、讨论、论著」，来自 tractare「处理、商谈」，是 trahere「拉、引」的反复动词。

items.en: Old French traite or traité named a negotiated agreement, and English treaty followed that diplomatic sense.
items.cn: 古法语 traite 或 traité 指谈成的协议，英语 treaty 沿用了这一外交义。

items.en: Peace treaty became a standard collocation in European diplomacy from the seventeenth century onward; its exact first use is not fixed.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，peace treaty 成为欧洲外交的标准搭配；其确切首用不明。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation and deeper roots): dictionaries disagree on the first English use of the phrase, and the proposed Indo-European root of pax is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：辞书对短语最早的英语用例说法不一，且为 pax 提出的印欧词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds treaty-family words easily confused with it; group two holds the neighbouring settlement ideas.
note.cn: 第一组是易与它混淆的条约类词；第二组是邻近的解决方案概念。

entries.definition: Any binding agreement between states; a peace treaty is the species that ends a war.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家间任何有约束力的协定；和平条约是其中结束战争的那一类。

entries.definition: A long formal writing on a subject; it shares the Latin root but means a book, not a bargain.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于某主题的长篇正式著述；同出拉丁词根，但指书，不指协议。

entries.definition: A compact or agreement, often narrower and less ceremonial than a treaty.
entries.definitionCN: 指约定或协议，通常比条约更窄、更少仪式性。

entries.definition: A suspension of hostilities; it precedes a peace treaty and does not settle the war.
entries.definitionCN: 指暂停敌对行动；它先于和平条约，并不解决战争。

entries.definition: An agreed stop in firing; it can be local and temporary, with no postwar settlement.
entries.definitionCN: 指约定的停止射击；可局部、临时，不含战后安排。

entries.definition: The substantive resolution of a dispute; a treaty is one legal form a settlement can take.
entries.definitionCN: 指争端的实质解决；条约是解决方案可采用的一种法律形式。

entries.definition: A formal agreement, often used for arms control or trade rather than for ending a war.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式协议，常用于军控或贸易，而非结束战争。

entries.definition: A surrender on terms; it can precede a treaty but is imposed by the stronger side.
entries.definitionCN: 指按条件投降；它可能先于条约，但由较强一方强加。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin roots, the diplomatic phrases and the distinction from a mere ceasefire.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁词根、外交搭配，以及它与单纯停火的区别。

normal.en: pax 'peace' + tractatus 'negotiation': a negotiated peace.
normal.cn: pax「和平」+ tractatus「商谈」：谈成的和平。

normal.en: Peace goes through Old French pais; treaty through Old French traite.
normal.cn: peace 经古法语 pais；treaty 经古法语 traite。

normal.en: The family runs peace, peaceful, pacify, pacific, pact, treaty, treatise.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 peace、peaceful、pacify、pacific、pact、treaty、treatise。

normal.en: A ceasefire stops the guns; a peace treaty ends the war.
normal.cn: 停火让枪停下；和平条约结束战争。

normal.en: Fixed partners: sign, negotiate, terms, violate.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：签署、谈判、条款、违反。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint drawn after the rubble, not during the shelling.
abstract.cn: 想象一张在瓦砾之后而非炮击之中画出的蓝图。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge whose planks are clauses; trust is the traffic that later uses it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，桥板是条款，信任是日后行驶其上的车流。

abstract.en: Picture two exhausted neighbours drawing a line they both promise to respect.
abstract.cn: 想象两个疲惫的邻居画出双方都承诺尊重的一条线。

examples.en: The peace treaty recognised the new frontier but left the port disputed.
examples.cn: 和约承认了新边界，却把港口归属留作争议。

examples.en: A peace treaty was signed only after the armistice held for a year.
examples.cn: 停战维持一年之后，和平条约才得以签署。

examples.en: Historians argue that the peace treaty sowed the next war.
examples.cn: 历史学家认为，这份和约埋下了下一场战争的种子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「peace（和平）+ treaty（条约）」——把和平写进纸面的条约 → 和平条约

root: peace 经古法语来自拉丁 pax「和平、约定」；treaty 经古法语来自拉丁 tractatus「处理、商谈」，源于 tractare「处理」，是 trahere「拉、引」的反复动词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from the agreement that ends a war, through the paper and the ceremony, to the clauses and the postwar order, to types of settlement, and finally to any formal reconciliation and the frame it supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从结束战争的协定出发，经过文书与仪式，再到条款与战后秩序，再到解决方案类型，最后落到任何正式和解以及它提供的框架。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table, a thick document, two pens and guns falling silent outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌、一份厚文件、两支笔，窗外的枪声沉寂。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: the phrase is both the deal and the paper that carries it.
branches.cn: 工具：这个短语既指交易，也指承载它的纸。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE TEXT: signing is the moment, clauses are the substance.
branches.cn: 行为与文本：签署是时刻，条款是实质。

branches.en: THE ORDER: a settlement builds a postwar world, and its type depends on who signs.
branches.cn: 秩序：解决方案建立一个战后世界，其类型取决于签署者。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: a long private feud borrows the public instrument.
branches.cn: 比喻：长期私人争执借用这份公开文书。

branches.en: THE FRAME: the document supplies structure that trust may later inhabit.
branches.cn: 框架：文书提供结构，信任日后入住。

intro.en: Both words are Latin-derived and still build large families, so the phrase can be read through its two roots.
intro.cn: 两个词都源自拉丁语，且仍构成大词族，因此这个短语可沿两个词根读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin pax gives peace, pacify, pacific and pact; Latin tractare gives treaty, treat, treatise, tract and negotiate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pax 衍生 peace、pacify、pacific 与 pact；拉丁 tractare 衍生 treaty、treat、treatise、tract 与 negotiate。

items.structure: peace (Old French pais, from Latin pax)
items.meaning: the state of being free from war
items.example: The village had known peace for a generation.
items.exampleCN: 这个村庄已太平了一代人的时间。

items.example: Roman writers used pax for both truce and quiet.
items.exampleCN: 罗马作家用 pax 既指休战也指安宁。

items.example: Patrols tried to pacify the district.
items.exampleCN: 巡逻队试图平定这个地区。

items.example: The two states signed a pacific accord.
items.exampleCN: 两国签署了一项和平协定。

items.example: The pact limited naval tonnage.
items.exampleCN: 该协议限制了海军吨位。

items.example: The treaty opened two ports.
items.exampleCN: 条约开放了两个港口。

items.example: He wrote a treatise on fortification.
items.exampleCN: 他写了一部筑城学论著。

items.example: They negotiated for six months.
items.exampleCN: 他们谈判了六个月。

items.example: A peace agreement may fall short of a treaty.
items.exampleCN: 和平协议可能不及条约正式。

definition_zh: 历史冲突；历史上发生并留下长期影响的对抗，也指研究这类对抗的历史学领域
definition_en: an armed or political confrontation located in the past and studied for its long consequences
core_image: 旧地图上两种颜色的箭头在山口相撞，纸面留下折痕，旁边的档案盒按年份排开
scene: 档案馆的阅览桌上摊着一张旧地图，两种颜色的箭头在山口相遇，旁边摆着同一场战事的往来文书。Historians treat the frontier dispute as a historical conflict, a past confrontation studied for its long consequences, shaped by drought and migration.
sceneCN: 这里 historical conflict 指「发生在过去、并留下长期影响的对抗」（第 1 个义项：被当作历史对象研究的冲突）；句意为历史学家把这场边境争端视为由旱灾与迁徙塑造的历史冲突。可辨识物件：旧地图、两色箭头、档案盒、往来文书、阅览桌台灯。

pos.zh: 历史冲突；历史上的对抗（可数，复数 historical conflicts）

collocations.phrase: the legacy of a historical conflict

senses.title: A past armed confrontation
senses.definition: an armed struggle that took place in the past and is now studied as history
senses.definitionCN: 发生在过去、如今作为历史来研究的武装斗争
senses.example: Historians treat the frontier dispute as a historical conflict shaped by drought and migration.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把这场边境争端视为由旱灾与迁徙塑造的历史冲突。
senses.why: historical places the event in the past, and conflict names the clash, so the phrase is a clash seen through time.
senses.whyCN: historical 把事件放进过去，conflict 指碰撞，因此短语是「透过时间看见的碰撞」。

senses.title: A particular war or campaign
senses.definition: a named war, campaign or battle treated as a historical event
senses.definitionCN: 作为历史事件处理的具名战争、战役或会战
senses.example: The siege is taught as a defining historical conflict of the dynasty.
senses.exampleCN: 这场围城被视为该王朝具有决定意义的历史冲突来讲授。
senses.why: once a single event acquires a name and a date, it becomes a unit in the historical record.
senses.whyCN: 一旦单一事件有了名称与日期，它就成了历史记录中的一个单位。

senses.title: A long adversarial relationship
senses.definition: a prolonged confrontation between states or groups, such as a cold war, without a single decisive battle
senses.definitionCN: 国家或群体之间长期的对峙，如冷战，没有单一决战
senses.example: Their rivalry is a historical conflict that outlasted three treaties.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的对抗是一场经历了三个条约仍未结束的历史冲突。
senses.why: conflict also names a state of opposition, not only a fight, so the phrase covers decades of tension.
senses.whyCN: conflict 也指对立状态，不只是打斗，因此这个短语涵盖数十年的紧张。

senses.title: A social or political conflict in history
senses.titleCN: 历史上的社会或政治冲突
senses.definition: a past struggle over class, religion, region or rights, whether or not it was fought with arms
senses.definitionCN: 过去围绕阶级、宗教、地区或权利的斗争，无论是否动武
senses.example: The land reform is studied as a historical conflict between two rural orders.
senses.exampleCN: 土地改革被研究为两种乡村秩序之间的历史冲突。
senses.why: the phrase is not limited to armies; any deep social cleavage can be historical conflict.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语不限于军队；任何深刻的社会分裂都可成为历史冲突。

senses.title: The academic field of conflict history
senses.titleCN: 历史学中的冲突研究领域
senses.definition: the scholarly study of how past conflicts began, unfolded and were remembered
senses.definitionCN: 研究过去冲突如何发生、展开与被记忆的学术领域
senses.example: Her chair is in historical conflict studies.
senses.exampleCN: 她的教席属于历史冲突研究。
senses.why: a phrase naming a class of events can also name the field that studies that class, as with memory studies.
senses.whyCN: 命名一类事件的短语也能命名研究该类的领域，如记忆研究。

senses.title: Contested memory and narrative
senses.definition: the struggle between groups over how a past conflict should be told and commemorated
senses.definitionCN: 群体之间关于过去冲突应如何讲述与纪念的争夺
senses.example: The monument turned the war into a historical conflict still being argued over.
senses.exampleCN: 这座纪念碑把那场战争变成一场仍在争论中的历史冲突。
senses.why: history is written after the guns stop, so a conflict can continue as a quarrel over its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 历史写成于枪声之后，因此冲突可以继续为对意义的争执。

senses.title: Figurative long-running dispute
senses.definition: by extension, any prolonged non-military quarrel treated as if it were history
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何被当作历史来对待的长期非军事争执
senses.example: The two journals waged a historical conflict over the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 两份期刊围绕这批档案展开了一场「历史冲突」。
senses.why: the metaphor lends dignity and duration to a dispute by calling it historical.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻通过称争执为「历史的」，赋予它体面与漫长时间。

senses.title: Abstraction: tension between interpretations
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：解释之间的张力
senses.definition: the unresolved tension between competing interpretations of the same past
senses.definitionCN: 对同一过去存在相互竞争的解释时未消解的张力
senses.example: Every archive holds a historical conflict between silence and testimony.
senses.exampleCN: 每座档案馆都藏着一场沉默与证词之间的历史冲突。
senses.why: at the deepest level the clash is between accounts, not armies: interpretation itself can be the contested ground.
senses.whyCN: 最深层的碰撞发生在叙述之间，而非军队之间：解释本身就能成为争夺之地。

intro.en: Historical comes from Greek historia 'inquiry' through Latin; conflict comes from Latin confligere 'to strike together'. The phrase is an English academic collocation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: historical 经拉丁语来自希腊 historia「探究」；conflict 来自拉丁 confligere「一起撞击」。短语是英语学术搭配。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek historia meant 'inquiry, account, narrative'; it came from histōr 'witness, learned man', connected to a root for knowing that is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 希腊 historia 意为「探究、记述、叙述」；来自 histōr「见证者、博学者」，与一个表示「知道」的词根相关，该词根属重构而非有记录。

items.en: Latin historicus was used for narrative accounts and for writers of them; English historical took this line and later added the sense of 'belonging to the past'.
items.cn: 拉丁 historicus 用于叙事记述及其作者；英语 historical 沿此线发展，后来增添「属于过去」之义。

items.en: Confligere meant 'to strike together, clash', built from com- 'together' and fligere 'to strike'.
items.cn: confligere 意为「一起撞击、冲突」，由 com-「一起」与 fligere「击打」构成。

items.en: The past participle conflictus named a collision or struggle, and English conflict came through French from that form.
items.cn: 过去分词 conflictus 指碰撞或斗争，英语 conflict 经法语来自这一形式。

items.en: Historical conflict became a common academic label in history and political science in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; its exact first use is not recorded.
items.cn: historical conflict 在十九、二十世纪成为历史学与政治学的常见学术标签；其确切首用不明。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation and root shapes): no dictionary fixes the first use of the phrase; the root behind histōr and the deeper origin of fligere are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根形态）：没有辞书确定该短语的首次使用；histōr 背后的词根与 fligere 的更深来源均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds history-family words that are routinely confused with historical conflict; group two holds neighbouring ideas about clashes.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 historical conflict 混淆的历史类词；第二组是关于碰撞的邻近概念。

entries.definition: Historic means important in history; historical means belonging to history. A historic conflict is a celebrated one, not simply an old one.
entries.definitionCN: historic 指历史上重要的；historical 指属于历史的。historic conflict 指著名的冲突，而不只是古老的冲突。

entries.definition: Any past occurrence studied by historians; a conflict is one kind of event, not the whole class.
entries.definitionCN: 指历史学家研究的任何过去事件；冲突是其中一类，而非全部。

entries.definition: The study of conflicts over time; the order of the words marks it as a discipline rather than a single clash.
entries.definitionCN: 指对冲突的历时研究；词序表明它是学科，而非单次碰撞。

entries.definition: Organized armed fighting between states; it is narrower than conflict, which also covers political and social clashes.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家间有组织的武装战斗；比 conflict 窄，后者也涵盖政治与社会碰撞。

entries.definition: The way a society remembers past events; it is the frame through which a historical conflict is understood.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会记住过去事件的方式；它是理解历史冲突的框架。

entries.definition: A war between groups within one state; it is a species of historical conflict with a defined legal shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指一国之内群体间的战争；是历史冲突的一种，具有明确的法律形态。

entries.definition: A quarrel over a frontier; it can become a historical conflict but may remain diplomatic.
entries.definitionCN: 指围绕边界的争执；它可演变成历史冲突，也可能停留在外交层面。

entries.definition: The enduring effects of a past clash; it describes the aftermath, not the clash itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指过去碰撞的持久影响；描述后果，而非碰撞本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two roots, the historic-historical distinction and the real archival setting.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个词根、historic 与 historical 的区别，以及真实的档案场景。

normal.en: historia 'inquiry' + confligere 'strike together': a past clash that people inquire into.
normal.cn: historia「探究」+ confligere「一起撞击」：人们去探究的过去碰撞。

normal.en: Historic means famous in history; historical means belonging to the past.
normal.cn: historic 指历史上著名；historical 指属于过去。

normal.en: The family runs history, historic, historical, historian, conflict, conflicting, afflict.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 history、historic、historical、historian、conflict、conflicting、afflict。

normal.en: conflict is com- 'together' plus fligere 'strike': two forces hitting at once.
normal.cn: conflict 是 com-「一起」加 fligere「击打」：两股力量同时相撞。

normal.en: Memory is part of the subject: a conflict continues in how it is told.
normal.cn: 记忆也是研究对象：冲突会以讲述方式继续存在。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows on an old map that keep meeting whenever the map is unfolded.
abstract.cn: 想象旧地图上的两支箭头，每次展开地图都会再次相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a scar that outlasts the wound and changes how the body moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一道比伤口更持久的疤，改变了身体的动作。

abstract.en: Picture two witnesses of one event telling stories that cannot both be true.
abstract.cn: 想象同一事件的两位见证者讲出无法同时成立的故事。

examples.en: The course compares historical conflicts across three continents.
examples.cn: 这门课程比较三大洲的历史冲突。

examples.en: A historical conflict can shape borders long after the fighting stops.
examples.cn: 历史冲突在战斗停止很久之后仍能塑造边界。

examples.en: The museum avoids turning a historical conflict into a simple hero story.
examples.cn: 博物馆避免把一场历史冲突简化为英雄故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「history（历史）+ conflict（冲突）」——写进历史书里的那场对抗 → 历史冲突

root: historical 经拉丁 historicus 来自希腊 historia「探究、记述」，histōr 为「见证者」；conflict 来自拉丁 confligere「一起撞击」= com-（一起）+ fligere（击打），经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from a past armed clash, through a named war and a long rivalry, to social struggles and the academic field, then to contested memory, a figurative feud and finally a tension between interpretations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从过去的武装碰撞出发，经过具名战争与长期对抗，再到社会斗争与学术领域，再到记忆争夺、比喻性争执，最后落到解释之间的张力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two coloured arrows meeting at a mountain pass on an old map, folded and refolded along the line of contact.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧地图上两支彩色箭头在山口相遇，沿接触线被反复折叠。

branches.en: THE EVENT: a dated clash becomes a unit of history.
branches.cn: 事件：有日期的碰撞成为历史的一个单位。

branches.en: THE LONG STRETCH: rivalry and social cleavage last beyond any single battle.
branches.cn: 长时段：对抗与社会分裂超越任何单场战斗。

branches.en: THE STUDY AND ITS OBJECTION: historians study the clash, and later groups argue over its meaning.
branches.cn: 研究及其异议：历史学家研究碰撞，后来的群体争夺其意义。

branches.en: BORROWED DURATION: a private feud gains historical weight by borrowing the phrase.
branches.cn: 借来的时长：私人争执借这个短语获得历史分量。

branches.en: INTERPRETIVE TENSION: the deepest clash is between accounts of the same past.
branches.cn: 解释张力：最深的碰撞发生在对同一过去的叙述之间。

intro.en: Both words are learned borrowings with productive roots, so the phrase reads as inquiry plus collision.
intro.cn: 两个词都是学术借词，词根能产，因此这个短语可读作「探究加碰撞」。

latinIntro.en: Greek historia reached Latin as historia and gives history, historian and historical; Latin fligere gives conflict, afflict and inflict.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 historia 进入拉丁作 historia，衍生 history、historian 与 historical；拉丁 fligere 衍生 conflict、afflict 与 inflict。

items.example: History is written from surviving traces.
items.exampleCN: 历史依据留存痕迹写成。

items.meaning: belonging to or studied as history
items.meaningCN: 属于历史或作为历史研究的
items.example: The archive is a historical source.
items.exampleCN: 这批档案是历史资料。

items.example: The ruling was a historic moment.
items.exampleCN: 这项裁决是一个历史性时刻。

items.example: The historian checked three archives.
items.exampleCN: 历史学家查证了三座档案馆。

items.example: The conflict lasted a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这场冲突持续了十年。

items.example: The Latin verb pictured two forces meeting.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词描绘两股力量相遇。

items.example: Famine afflicted the valley for years.
items.exampleCN: 饥荒折磨这个谷地多年。

items.example: The treaty inflicted heavy terms on the loser.
items.exampleCN: 条约把苛刻条款加给战败方。

items.example: The reports gave conflicting accounts.
items.exampleCN: 这些报告给出了相互矛盾的说法。

latinEntries.structure: historia, historiae (f., first declension; from Greek)
historicus, historici (m., second declension; from Greek)

definition_zh: 迫害；因宗教、政治或族群身份而遭受的系统性打压；迫害行为或迫害时期
definition_en: systematic, often prolonged mistreatment of a group because of its religion, politics, ethnicity or other identity
core_image: 一扇被砸开的门，屋内书页散落，墙上有炭笔写的警告，窗外有人低头快步走过
scene: 旧城巷口，一群人的门被做了记号，夜里传来砸门声，邻居把窗帘拉紧，不敢点灯。The diary records the persecution, the systematic pursuit that drove the family from the city because of its faith.
sceneCN: 这里 persecution 指「因身份而遭受的系统性打压」（第 1 个义项：持续且有目标的迫害）；句意为日记记录了迫使这家人离开城市的迫害。可辨识物件：门上的记号、散落书页、紧拉的窗帘、黑暗的窗口。

pos.zh: 迫害；迫害行为或时期（可数，复数 persecutions；不可数时指整体现象）

senses.title: Systematic persecution of a group
senses.definition: prolonged, organized mistreatment of people because of religion, politics, ethnicity or another identity
senses.definitionCN: 因宗教、政治、族群或其他身份而有组织地长期虐待一群人
senses.example: The diary records the persecution that drove the family from the city.
senses.exampleCN: 日记记录了迫使这家人离开城市的迫害。
senses.why: persecutio is a following-through: per- 'through' plus sequi 'follow', so the word pictures a pursuit that does not stop.
senses.whyCN: persecutio 是「一路跟到底」：per-「贯穿」加 sequi「跟随」，因此这个词描绘一种不肯停下的追逼。

senses.title: A single act or incident
senses.definition: one concrete act of harassment, arrest, seizure or violence aimed at a group's member
senses.definitionCN: 针对群体成员的一次具体骚扰、逮捕、查抄或暴力行为
senses.example: Each persecution was logged by the court clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次迫害都被法庭书记记录下来。
senses.why: a long campaign is made of separate blows, and English lets the countable plural name those blows.
senses.whyCN: 长期运动由一次次打击构成，英语用可数复数来命名这些打击。

senses.title: A period or state of persecution
senses.definition: the span of time in which a group lives under systematic pressure
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体在系统性压力下生活的那段时间
senses.example: The persecution lasted three decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这场迫害持续了三十年。
senses.why: the noun can name a stretch of time, like reign or famine, because the condition has a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 和统治期、饥荒一样，这个名词可指一段时间，因为这种状态有始有终。

senses.title: Legal and administrative persecution
senses.titleCN: 法律与行政手段的迫害
senses.definition: the use of registration, permits, courts or police powers to isolate and punish a group
senses.definitionCN: 利用登记、许可、法庭或警权来隔离并惩罚某一群体
senses.example: Registration rules turned into a form of persecution.
senses.exampleCN: 登记规则变成了一种迫害形式。
senses.why: persecution needs no uniformed mob; paperwork can pursue people just as effectively.
senses.whyCN: 迫害不需要暴民；纸面手续同样能有效追逼人。

senses.title: Social ostracism by a community
senses.definition: non-state exclusion through rumour, boycott, denial of work or housing
senses.definitionCN: 通过流言、抵制、拒绝工作或住房而实施的非国家排斥
senses.example: Persecution can begin with a whisper in the schoolyard.
senses.exampleCN: 迫害可以始于校园里的一句悄悄话。
senses.why: the pursuit can be carried out by neighbours rather than officials, which is why the word covers social pressure.
senses.whyCN: 这种追逼可由邻里而非官员实施，因此这个词也涵盖社会压力。

senses.title: Historical name for a specific persecution
senses.definition: the capitalized name given to a particular official campaign, such as the Great Persecution
senses.definitionCN: 对某次官方运动的专名，如「大迫害」
senses.example: Historians date the Great Persecution to the reign of Diocletian.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把「大迫害」定在戴克里先统治时期。
senses.why: major campaigns receive proper names, and the common noun becomes part of a historical label.
senses.whyCN: 重大运动获得专名，普通名词便成为历史标签的一部分。

senses.title: Figurative campaign against a view or group
senses.titleCN: 比喻：对某种观点或群体的围攻
senses.definition: by extension, organized hostility toward a belief, profession or faction outside state action
senses.definitionCN: 引申指国家行为之外，对某种信念、职业或派别的有组织敌意
senses.example: Scientists described the campaign as a persecution of dissent.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家把这场运动称为对不同意见的迫害。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the asymmetry: one side pursues, the other cannot rest.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了不对称：一方追逼，另一方不得安宁。

senses.title: Abstraction: pursuit that gives no rest
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不容对方喘息的追逼
senses.definition: any sustained pressure by a stronger party that denies a weaker party safety or peace
senses.definitionCN: 强者对弱者施加、使其失去安全或安宁的持续压力
senses.example: Persecution is pursuit that refuses to let its object rest.
senses.exampleCN: 迫害是不让对象安歇的那种追逼。
senses.why: the root sense of following explains the whole family of meanings: persecution is not one blow but an ongoing chase.
senses.whyCN: 词根的「跟随」义解释了整个词义家族：迫害不是一击，而是持续的追赶。

intro.en: Persecution comes from Latin persequi 'to follow through, pursue', built on per- 'through' and sequi 'to follow'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: persecution 来自拉丁 persequi「一路跟随、追逼」，由 per-「贯穿」与 sequi「跟随」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Persequi meant 'to follow persistently, pursue, hunt down'; the prefix per- adds the idea of carrying the action through to the end.
items.cn: persequi 意为「持续跟随、追捕、追到底」；前缀 per- 增添「把动作做到底」的意思。

items.en: Sequi meant 'to follow'; its Indo-European ancestor is usually reconstructed as *sekʷ-, a reconstruction and not a recorded form.
items.cn: sequi 意为「跟随」；其印欧祖形通常重构为 *sekʷ-，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Persecutio named a pursuit or a following after; in late Latin legal and church writing it took on the sense of hostile pursuit.
items.cn: persecutio 指追赶或追随；在晚期拉丁语的法律与教会写作中，它带上敌意追逼之义。

items.en: Old French persecution carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in religious contexts.
items.cn: 古法语 persecution 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初用于宗教语境。

items.en: The organized sense grew in accounts of martyrs and later in political writing about minorities and dissent.
items.cn: 有组织的迫害义先在殉道者记述中成长，后来进入关于少数群体与异议的政治写作。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English citation and root shape): dictionaries differ on the earliest English use, and the Indo-European form behind sequi is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与词根形态）：辞书对最早的英语用例说法不一，sequi 背后的印欧形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same following root that are constantly confused with persecution; group two holds neighbouring terms for organised mistreatment.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「跟随」词根、常与 persecution 混淆的词；第二组是有组织的虐待类邻近词。

entries.definition: From pro- 'forward' plus sequi: the state's pursuit of a case in court. It shares the root but names legal action, not group mistreatment.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 pro-「向前」加 sequi：国家在法庭上追究案件。同词根，但指法律诉讼，不指群体虐待。

entries.definition: To follow in order to catch; it has no built-in idea of injustice or group identity.
entries.definitionCN: 指为抓住而追赶；本身不含不义或群体身份之意。

entries.definition: To subject someone to persecution; the noun names the campaign, the verb names the repeated act.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某人实施迫害；名词指运动，动词指反复的行为。

entries.definition: The person or body that carries out persecution; it names the pursuer rather than the pursuit.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施迫害的人或机构；命名追逼者而非追逼本身。

entries.definition: Unjust exercise of power that weighs a group down; persecution stresses the chase, oppression stresses the burden.
entries.definitionCN: 指不义地行使权力压住群体；persecution 强调追逼，oppression 强调重压。

entries.definition: Differential treatment based on identity; it can exist without an active campaign of pursuit.
entries.definitionCN: 指基于身份的区别对待；可以没有主动追逼的运动而存在。

entries.definition: An organised mass attack on a particular community, often short and violent; persecution may last much longer.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某一社群的有机组织的大规模攻击，常短促而暴力；迫害可持续更久。

entries.definition: Repeated unwanted pressure on a person; it can be individual and need not target a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指对个人反复施加的不受欢迎压力；可针对个人，不必针对群体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: per- plus sequi, the shared root family and the historical proper name.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：per- 加 sequi、同根词族，以及那个历史专名。

normal.en: per- 'through' + sequi 'follow': to follow someone through every door they enter.
normal.cn: per-「贯穿」+ sequi「跟随」：跟着一个人穿过他所进的每一道门。

normal.en: The family runs persecute, persecution, persecutor, prosecute, prosecution, pursue.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 persecute、persecution、persecutor、prosecute、prosecution、pursue。

normal.en: prosecution is pro- 'forward': the court pushes a case forward, a different direction from persecution.
normal.cn: prosecution 是 pro-「向前」：法庭把案件向前推，与迫害的方向不同。

normal.en: The Great Persecution is dated to Diocletian's reign, early in the fourth century.
normal.cn: 「大迫害」定在四世纪初的戴克里先统治时期。

normal.en: Typical partners are flee, escape, campaign of and systematic.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「逃离」「躲避」「一场……运动」与「系统性的」。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that follows a person from room to room and never sleeps.
abstract.cn: 想象一道影子跟着人从一个房间到另一个房间，从不睡觉。

abstract.en: Picture a net drawn tighter each time the caught thing moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，被捕获之物每动一下，网就收紧一分。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a list that is checked at every door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写进名单，每道门口都要核对。

examples.en: Many families fled the persecution and crossed the border at night.
examples.cn: 许多家庭逃离迫害，在夜里越过边境。

examples.en: The law turned ordinary paperwork into an instrument of persecution.
examples.cn: 这项法律把普通文书变成了迫害工具。

examples.en: Survivors gave testimony about persecution that lasted for years.
examples.cn: 幸存者就持续多年的迫害作证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「per（一直）+ secu（跟随）」——一直跟着某群人追打 → 迫害

root: 拉丁 persequi「追到底」= per-（贯穿）+ sequi「跟随」；名词 persecutio 指追逼。sequi 的印欧祖形 *sekʷ- 属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one chase: a group is pursued because of who it is. The chase becomes single acts, a long period, legal machinery, social exclusion, a named historical campaign, a metaphor for hostility to ideas and finally the pure shape of pursuit without rest.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一场追逼展开：一群人因其身份而被追赶。这场追逼先成为单次行为，再成为长时期，再成为法律机器、社会排斥、具名的历史运动、对观念的敌意比喻，最后成为「不容喘息」的追逼本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked door, scattered pages and footsteps that keep coming back at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：被做了记号的门、散落的书页，以及夜里反复回来的脚步声。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: the chase lasts long enough to become a period of life.
branches.cn: 运动：追逼持续到足以成为一段生活时期。

branches.en: THE BLOW AND THE FORM: one act, then a system of rules that repeats it.
branches.cn: 打击与形式：先是一次行为，再是一套重复它的规则。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND THE RECORD: neighbours join in, and major campaigns receive names.
branches.cn: 社会与记录：邻里参与，重大运动获得名称。

branches.en: THE BORROWED CHASE: hostility toward a view borrows the shape of persecution.
branches.cn: 借来的追逼：对某种观点的敌意借用了迫害的形状。

branches.en: NO REST: the root idea of following explains why the word implies endless pressure.
branches.cn: 不得安歇：词根的「跟随」解释了为何这个词暗示无尽的压力。

intro.en: Persecution is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin root and a noun suffix, all of which still build English words.
intro.cn: persecution 由拉丁前缀、拉丁词根与名词后缀构成，三者仍构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi gives pursue, pursue's relatives, prosecute and sequence; per- adds the sense of going through to the end.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sequi 衍生 pursue、prosecute 与 sequence；per- 增添「做到底」的意思。

items.example: The prefix turns following into a chase to the finish.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「跟随」变成追到底。

items.example: The root is the plain act of following.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是「跟随」这个动作。

items.example: The Latin verb implied no rest for the pursued.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词暗示被追者不得安歇。

items.example: Persecution is organized, not accidental.
items.exampleCN: 迫害是有组织的，而非偶然的。

items.example: The regime persecuted the community for years.
items.exampleCN: 该政权迫害这个社群多年。

items.example: The persecutor kept a list of names.
items.exampleCN: 迫害者保存着一份名单。

items.meaning: to follow a case forward in court
items.example: The state prosecuted the officials.
items.exampleCN: 国家起诉了这些官员。

items.meaning: the conduct of a legal case
items.example: The prosecution called three witnesses.
items.exampleCN: 检方传唤了三名证人。

items.structure: pursue (Old French poursivre, from Latin prosequi)
items.meaning: to follow in order to catch
items.example: The patrol pursued the group for two days.
items.exampleCN: 巡逻队追赶这群人两天。

items.example: The events formed a clear sequence.
items.exampleCN: 这些事件形成清晰的顺序。
