definition_zh: 压迫；不义的统治或制度性压制；沉重压抑的感受
definition_en: the unjust or cruel exercise of power over a group, or the heavy sense of being weighed down
core_image: 一盘沉重的石磨压在一排肩上，磨盘下的地面被压出深深的凹痕
scene: 工厂门口，工人排成长队等候检查，守卫把证件扔回他们脸上，午后的热气压在低矮的屋顶下。The novel describes the oppression, the unjust weight of rule that kept the whole district silent.
sceneCN: 这里 oppression 指「制度性的不义压制」（第 1 个义项：长期施于群体的沉重统治）；句意为小说描写了让整个街区噤声的那种压迫。可辨识物件：工厂门、长队、证件、守卫、低矮屋顶下的热气。

pos.zh: 压迫；压制；压抑感（可数，复数 oppressions）

senses.title: Systematic unjust rule over a group
senses.titleCN: 对群体的系统性不义统治
senses.definition: the prolonged, unjust exercise of power that keeps a group down
senses.definitionCN: 长期不义地行使权力，使一个群体处于低下地位
senses.example: The novel describes the oppression that kept the whole district silent.
senses.exampleCN: 小说描写了让整个街区噤声的那种压迫。
senses.why: opprimere is ob- 'against' plus premere 'press': power is pressed down on someone until they cannot rise.
senses.whyCN: opprimere 是 ob-「对着」加 premere「压」：权力压在某人身上，直到他起不来。

senses.title: A heavy feeling of being weighed down
senses.definition: a bodily or mental sense of heaviness, tightness or suffocation
senses.definitionCN: 身体或心理上沉重、紧绷或窒息的感受
senses.example: A sudden oppression in the chest made him sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 胸口突然一阵压抑，使他坐了下来。
senses.why: the physical image of pressing explains the feeling: something invisible sits on the breath.
senses.whyCN: 「压」的身体意象解释了这种感受：有某种无形之物压住了呼吸。

senses.title: A specific oppressive act or measure
senses.titleCN: 具体的压迫行为或措施
senses.definition: one law, order or action that imposes unjust burden on people
senses.definitionCN: 给人们施加不义负担的一项法律、命令或行动
senses.example: Each oppression was recorded in the parish ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次压迫都被记在教区账簿里。
senses.why: a system is made of measures, and the countable plural names them one by one.
senses.whyCN: 制度由措施构成，可数复数把它们逐条命名。

senses.title: Economic oppression
senses.definition: exploitative wages, debt, rents or exclusion that keep people poor by design
senses.definitionCN: 有意使人贫穷的剥削性工资、债务、租金或排斥
senses.example: Debt peonage was an economic oppression dressed as contract.
senses.exampleCN: 债务劳役是披着契约外衣的经济压迫。
senses.why: pressure can be applied through prices and contracts, not only through police.
senses.whyCN: 压力可以通过价格与契约施加，而不只是通过警察。

senses.title: Gender or ethnic oppression
senses.definition: structural disadvantage imposed on people because of gender, caste, ethnicity or similar identity
senses.definitionCN: 因性别、种姓、族群等身份而强加的结构性劣势
senses.example: The report documented the oppression of migrant women.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了对移民女性的压迫。
senses.why: the same heavy hand can target a category rather than an individual, which is why the word pairs with identity terms.
senses.whyCN: 同一只重手可以针对一个类别而非个人，因此这个词常与身份词搭配。

senses.title: A historical oppressive regime
senses.definition: a named colonial, caste or authoritarian order studied as a system
senses.definitionCN: 被作为制度研究的殖民、种姓或专制秩序
senses.example: Scholars compare the oppression of two colonial administrations.
senses.exampleCN: 学者比较两套殖民行政的压迫方式。
senses.why: historians treat oppression as an institutional design, not only as individual cruelty.
senses.whyCN: 历史学家把压迫当作制度设计，而不只是个人残忍。

senses.title: Metaphor: psychological or environmental weight
senses.titleCN: 比喻：心理或环境的重压
senses.definition: by extension, any atmosphere or mood that makes people feel small and tired
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何使人感到渺小而疲惫的气氛或情绪
senses.example: A grey sky added its own oppression to the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 灰暗的天空给这个下午添了一层自己的压抑。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers the stone's weight to air, light and mood.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把石头的重量转移到空气、光线与情绪上。

senses.title: Abstraction: any force that contracts freedom
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：收缩自由的力量
senses.definition: any structure or pressure that narrows a person's or group's room to act
senses.definitionCN: 任何缩小个人或群体行动空间的结构或压力
senses.example: Oppression is freedom compressed until it cannot breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 压迫是被压缩到无法呼吸的自由。
senses.why: the deepest sense is spatial: the hand does not only hurt, it reduces the space in which one can move.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是空间性的：那只手不仅造成疼痛，还缩小了可行动的空间。

intro.en: Oppression comes from Latin opprimere, ob- 'against' plus premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oppression 来自拉丁 opprimere，由 ob-「对着」与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Opprimere meant 'to press against, crush, overwhelm', built from ob- 'against, toward' and premere 'to press'.
items.cn: opprimere 意为「压向、压碎、压倒」，由 ob-「对着、朝向」与 premere「压」构成。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze'; its deeper origin is usually reconstructed with a root for striking, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤」；其更深来源通常以一个表示「击打」的词根重构，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Oppressio named a pressing down or crushing; the noun carried the physical weight of the verb into abstract use.
items.cn: oppressio 指压下或压碎；这个名词把动词的身体重量带入抽象用法。

items.en: Oppression entered English through Old French in the fourteenth century, first as a general word for crushing or burden.
items.cn: oppression 在十四世纪经古法语进入英语，最初泛指压碎或重负。

items.en: The political sense of unjust rule took shape in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and dominates modern usage.
items.cn: 不义统治的政治义在十七、十八世纪成形，并主导现代用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (political sense date and root shape): the exact point at which the word became primarily political is not fixed, and the pre-Latin root of premere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（政治义年代与词根形态）：这个词何时主要转为政治义并无定论，premere 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds press-root words that are easily swapped with oppression; group two holds neighbouring ideas of unjust power.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「压」词根、易与 oppression 互换的词；第二组是不义权力的邻近概念。

entries.definition: From sub- 'down' plus premere: the act of putting something down by force, such as a revolt or a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 sub-「向下」加 premere：以武力压下某物，如叛乱或事实。

entries.definition: From re- 'back' plus premere: keeping something from emerging, often used for impulses or dissent.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 re-「向后」加 premere：阻止某物浮现，常用于冲动或异议。

entries.definition: From de- 'down' plus premere: a lowered state, whether of ground, economy or mood. It is not a political term.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 de-「向下」加 premere：被压低的状态，可为地面、经济或情绪，并非政治术语。

entries.definition: From com- 'together' plus premere: squeezing into less space, a physical rather than social process.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 com-「一起」加 premere：压进更小空间，是物理过程而非社会过程。

entries.definition: Cruel and arbitrary rule by one person or a small clique; oppression can be impersonal and institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 指一人或小集团的残暴专断统治；oppression 可以是非个人的、制度性的。

entries.definition: Taking advantage of people's labour or weakness for profit; it is one engine of economic oppression.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用他人劳动或弱点获利；它是经济压迫的一种引擎。

entries.definition: Treating people differently because of identity; it can occur without a heavy system of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指因身份而区别对待；可以没有沉重的统治体系。

entries.definition: The act of conquering and subjecting a people; it stresses the moment of defeat more than daily pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指征服并使一个民族臣服；更强调被击败的时刻，而非日常压力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the press-root family and the bodily image of weight.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、press 词根家族，以及「重量」的身体意象。

normal.en: ob- 'against' + premere 'press': a hand pressing against someone until they cannot stand.
normal.cn: ob-「对着」+ premere「压」：一只手压在人身上，直到他站不起来。

normal.en: The family runs press, pressure, compress, suppress, repress, depress, oppress.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 press、pressure、compress、suppress、repress、depress、oppress。

normal.en: The prefixes show direction: sub- down, re- back, de- down, com- together, ob- against.
normal.cn: 前缀显示方向：sub- 向下、re- 向后、de- 向下、com- 一起、ob- 对着。

normal.en: Oppression has both a political sense and a bodily sense of heavy breathing.
normal.cn: oppression 既有政治义，也有呼吸沉重的身体义。

normal.en: Typical partners are live under, escape, systematic and economic.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「生活在……之下」「逃离」「系统性的」与「经济的」。

abstract.en: Picture a stone lid placed over a pot so that nothing can rise out.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板盖住锅口，使任何东西都升不出来。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose walls move inward a little each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，墙壁每年向内挪一点。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that weighs a person every morning and never lets the needle fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一台每天早上称人的秤，指针从不肯下落。

examples.en: The characters speak quietly because oppression has taught them caution.
examples.cn: 人物说话很轻，因为压迫教会了他们谨慎。

examples.en: Economic oppression can outlast the laws that created it.
examples.cn: 经济压迫可能比造成它的法律活得更久。

examples.en: The painting conveys the oppression of a low ceiling and a grey light.
examples.cn: 这幅画传达了低矮天花板与灰光的压抑感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「op（对着）+ press（压）」——一直对着人往下压 → 压迫

root: 拉丁 opprimere「压向、压倒」= ob-（对着）+ premere（压）；名词 oppressio。premere 的更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one gesture: a weight is pressed down. The weight becomes a political system, then a bodily feeling, then single measures, then economic and identity-based forms, then a historical regime, then a mood and finally any narrowing of freedom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个动作展开：把重量压下去。这个重量先成为政治制度，再成为身体感受，再成为单项措施，再成为经济与身份形式，再成为历史政权，再成为气氛，最后成为对自由的任何收窄。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a millstone resting on a row of shoulders, the ground dented beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘石磨压在一排肩上，地面被压出凹痕。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM AND ITS MEASURES: rule is applied one order at a time.
branches.cn: 制度与措施：统治是按一条条命令施加的。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT FELT: the stone becomes breath, sky and mood.
branches.cn: 感到的重量：石头变成呼吸、天空与情绪。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL AND THE CATEGORY: money and identity are two faces of the same hand.
branches.cn: 物质与类别：金钱与身份是同一只手的两个面。

branches.en: THE REGIME: historians study oppression as an institutional design.
branches.cn: 政权：历史学家把压迫当作制度设计来研究。

branches.en: THE SHRUNKEN ROOM: the deepest sense is reduced space for action.
branches.cn: 收缩的房间：最深的一层是行动空间的缩小。

intro.en: Oppression is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb root, and the same root builds a whole family of pressing words in English.
intro.cn: oppression 是拉丁前缀加拉丁动词词根，同一词根在英语中构成整个「压」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere gives press, pressure, compress, suppress, repress and depress; ob- adds the sense of pressing against.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 premere 衍生 press、pressure、compress、suppress、repress 与 depress；ob- 增添「对着压」的意思。

items.example: The prefix gives the pressure a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给压力一个方向。

items.example: The root is the physical act of pressing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是「压」这个身体动作。

items.example: The Latin verb joined direction and weight.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词把方向与重量结合起来。

items.example: Oppression can be a policy, not only a temper.
items.exampleCN: 压迫可以是一项政策，而不只是脾气。

items.example: The rules oppressed the poorest tenants.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则压制了最贫穷的佃户。

items.example: The oppressor feared the square at noon.
items.exampleCN: 压迫者害怕正午的广场。

items.example: The heat was oppressive by ten o'clock.
items.exampleCN: 到十点，热气已经令人窒息。

items.example: Press the seal into the wax.
items.exampleCN: 把印章压进蜡里。

items.example: The officers suppressed the protest.
items.exampleCN: 官员镇压了抗议。

items.example: She repressed the urge to answer.
items.exampleCN: 她压下了回嘴的冲动。

definition_zh: 解放；使脱离控制、监禁或束缚；释放（气体等）；解放运动
definition_en: the act of setting someone free from control, confinement or a constraining condition
core_image: 牢门被推开，光从走廊尽头照进来，门槛上落着一串钥匙
scene: 清晨的营区大门被从里面推开，人们沿着泥路走出来，等在门外的家人举起写着名字的纸牌。The archive records the liberation of the camp, the act of setting the prisoners free, in the spring of nineteen forty-five.
sceneCN: 这里 liberation 指「使被关押者脱离控制」（第 1 个义项：把人从拘禁中放出）；句意为档案记录了那处营地在四五年春天获得解放。可辨识物件：推开的大门、泥路、姓名纸牌、走廊尽头的晨光、落在地上的钥匙。

pos.zh: 解放；释放；解放运动（可数，复数 liberations）

senses.title: The act of setting someone free
senses.titleCN: 使某人获得自由的行为
senses.definition: the act of releasing a person or people from confinement, control or servitude
senses.definitionCN: 把人从拘禁、控制或奴役中放出的行为
senses.example: The archive records the liberation of the camp in the spring of nineteen forty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 档案记录了那处营地在四五年春天获得解放。
senses.why: liberare is 'to make free', from liber 'free'; the noun names the moment the condition changes.
senses.whyCN: liberare 是「使自由」，来自 liber「自由的」；名词指状态改变的那一刻。

senses.title: Military liberation of a place
senses.definition: the recapture or freeing of a territory by armed force
senses.definitionCN: 以武力收复或解救一片地区
senses.example: The liberation of the port cut the enemy's supply line.
senses.exampleCN: 港口的解放切断了敌方的补给线。
senses.why: armies describe recapture as liberation when they are welcomed as freeing the inhabitants.
senses.whyCN: 当军队被视为解救居民时，他们就把收复称为解放。

senses.title: National or colonial liberation
senses.definition: the ending of foreign rule and the achievement of independence
senses.definitionCN: 结束外国统治并取得独立
senses.example: National liberation movements reshaped the map after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后，民族解放运动重划了地图。
senses.why: a people under external rule experiences the end of that rule as a release, so the word joins national claims.
senses.whyCN: 受外来统治的民族把统治的结束体验为释放，因此这个词与民族诉求结合。

senses.title: Social liberation of a group
senses.definition: the removal of legal and social restraints from a class, gender or minority
senses.definitionCN: 解除对某一阶级、性别或少数群体的法律与社会束缚
senses.example: The liberation of women from restrictive property laws took decades.
senses.exampleCN: 女性从限制性财产法中的解放花了数十年。
senses.why: the word is borrowed from physical release to describe the removal of legal chains.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从身体释放借来，用来描述法律锁链的解除。

senses.title: Personal or intellectual liberation
senses.definition: a private release from fear, habit, ignorance or an oppressive belief
senses.definitionCN: 个人从恐惧、习惯、无知或压抑性信念中解脱
senses.example: Learning to read was a personal liberation for him.
senses.exampleCN: 学会阅读对他而言是一种个人的解放。
senses.why: the outer act has an inner analogue: what holds a mind can also be opened.
senses.whyCN: 外在动作有内在对应：锁住心智的东西也能被打开。

senses.title: A liberation movement or organization
senses.definition: an organized political force that describes its goal as liberation
senses.definitionCN: 以解放为目标的组织化政治力量
senses.example: The liberation front controlled three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 解放阵线控制着三个省。
senses.why: when a cause organizes, the abstract noun becomes part of its name.
senses.whyCN: 当一项事业组织起来，抽象名词就成为其名称的一部分。

senses.title: Release of a substance, especially a gas
senses.definition: the freeing of a gas, energy or chemical from a bound state
senses.definitionCN: 使气体、能量或化学物质从束缚状态中释放
senses.example: The liberation of gas from the rock warned the miners.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石中气体的释出警告了矿工。
senses.why: chemistry uses the same word for physical freeing, which shows how literal the core sense remains.
senses.whyCN: 化学用同一个词指物理释放，可见核心义仍然很字面。

senses.title: Abstraction: removal of any constraint
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何束缚的解除
senses.definition: any process by which a limit on action is removed, whether physical, legal or mental
senses.definitionCN: 任何解除行动限制的过程，无论物理、法律或心理
senses.example: Liberation begins when a rule loses its power to frighten.
senses.exampleCN: 当一条规则失去吓人的力量，解放就开始了。
senses.why: the deepest sense is negative: not the gaining of something new but the lifting of a weight.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是否定性的：不是获得新东西，而是移走一份重量。

intro.en: Liberation comes from Latin liberare 'to set free', from liber 'free'. The Latin word liber also means 'book' but is a different word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: liberation 来自拉丁 liberare「使自由」，源于 liber「自由的」。拉丁语中 liber 也指「书」，但那是另一个词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, unrestricted'; it is a different word from liber 'book', which belongs to another stem.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、不受限制的」；它与表示「书」的 liber 是另一个词，属不同词干。

items.en: Liberare meant 'to set free, release, acquit'; it turned the adjective into an action.
items.cn: liberare 意为「使自由、释放、宣告无罪」；它把形容词变成动作。

items.en: Liberatio named a setting free or acquittal, and English liberation came from this noun.
items.cn: liberatio 指释放或宣告无罪，英语 liberation 来自这个名词。

items.en: The word entered English through Old French in the fifteenth century, first in legal and religious senses.
items.cn: 这个词在十五世纪经古法语进入英语，最初用于法律与宗教语境。

items.en: From the eighteenth century liberation was applied to nations, slaves and social classes, and the political sense now dominates.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，liberation 被用于民族、奴隶与社会阶级，政治义如今占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin): the deeper root of liber is often reconstructed with a sense such as 'to grow up', but no single reconstruction is proven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语前来源）：liber 的更深词根常被重构为带有「成长」之义的形状，但没有哪一种重构得到证明。

note.en: Group one holds liberty-family words easily confused with liberation; group two holds neighbouring ideas of being freed.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 liberation 混淆的自由类词；第二组是「获得自由」的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The condition of being free; liberation is the act or process that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指自由的状态；liberation 是产生这一状态的行为或过程。

entries.definition: Originally 'befitting a free man', now a political and social label; it does not mean the act of freeing.
entries.definitionCN: 原指「适合自由人的」，现为政治与社会标签；不表示「解放」这个动作。

entries.definition: One who liberates; the noun names the agent, while liberation names the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施解放的人；名词命名施动者，而 liberation 命名行为。

entries.definition: Being saved from danger or captivity; it stresses rescue from a threat more than the ending of a system.
entries.definitionCN: 指从危险或囚禁中被救出；更强调脱离威胁，而非终结制度。

entries.definition: The formal legal freeing of a person from slavery or authority; liberation is broader and can be military or personal.
entries.definitionCN: 指法律上正式使某人脱离奴役或支配；liberation 更宽，可指军事或个人层面的解放。

entries.definition: The state of a nation governing itself; liberation can be the struggle that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家自治的状态；liberation 可以是产生它的斗争。

entries.definition: The act of letting a person or thing go; it is physical and neutral, without the political weight of liberation.
entries.definitionCN: 指放开人或物；是物理性、中性的，没有 liberation 的政治分量。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being constrained; liberation is one route to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受约束的一般状态；liberation 是通向它的一条路径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective, the real family and the physical picture of an opening door.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：那个拉丁形容词、真实词族，以及「门被打开」的身体图景。

normal.en: liber 'free' + -ation: the act of making free.
normal.cn: liber「自由的」+ -ation：使自由的行为。

normal.en: The family runs liberate, liberator, liberty, liberal, liberation, deliver.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 liberate、liberator、liberty、liberal、liberation、deliver。

normal.en: Do not confuse liber 'free' with liber 'book': same spelling, different stem.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 liber「自由的」与 liber「书」：拼写相同，词干不同。

normal.en: The core picture is a door opened from the inside.
normal.cn: 核心图景是一扇从里面被打开的门。

normal.en: Typical partners are national, movement, war of and women's.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「民族的」「运动」「……战争」与「妇女的」。

abstract.en: Picture a key left on the threshold after the lock has already been opened.
abstract.cn: 想象锁已打开之后，钥匙留在门槛上。

abstract.en: Picture a window opened in a room that had forgotten the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一间忘了天空的房间被打开一扇窗。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that still exists but no longer makes anyone afraid.
abstract.cn: 想象一条仍然存在却不再让人害怕的规则。

examples.en: The city celebrated its liberation with a quiet procession.
examples.cn: 这座城市以一场安静的游行庆祝解放。

examples.en: Literacy brought a kind of liberation that no law could grant.
examples.cn: 识字带来一种法律无法给予的解放。

examples.en: The experiment measured the liberation of hydrogen from the sample.
examples.cn: 实验测量了样品中氢气的释放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「lib（自由 libr）+ eration（变成）」——把人变成自由的状态 → 解放

root: 拉丁 liber「自由的」+ -atio（行为名词）→ liberatio「释放」。拉丁语 liber 另指「书」，属不同词干；liber 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one opening: a door is unlocked. The opening becomes a military recapture, a national end of foreign rule, a social removal of restraints, a private release, an organized cause, a chemical freeing and finally the lifting of any limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次开启展开：门被打开。这次开启先成为军事收复，再成为民族结束外来统治，再成为社会束缚的解除，再成为个人解脱，再成为组织化事业，再成为化学释放，最后成为任何限制的移走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lock opened from within, light entering a long corridor, keys left on the sill.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁从里面被打开，光进入长走廊，钥匙留在窗台上。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL OPENING: a person or a place is released by force or by arrival.
branches.cn: 身体开启：一个人或一个地方因武力或到来而获释。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE CLAIM: a people or a class claims release from a system.
branches.cn: 集体诉求：一个民族或阶级要求从制度中释放。

branches.en: THE INNER DOOR: what confined a mind can also be opened.
branches.cn: 内门：困住心智的东西也能被打开。

branches.en: THE ORGANIZED CAUSE: the noun becomes a banner for a movement.
branches.cn: 组织化事业：这个名词成为运动旗帜。

branches.en: THE LIFTED WEIGHT: chemistry and abstraction both mean a restraint removed.
branches.cn: 移走的重量：化学与抽象义都指束缚被解除。

intro.en: Liberation is a Latin adjective turned into an action noun, and the same stem builds a large English family.
intro.cn: liberation 是由拉丁形容词变成的行为名词，同一词干构成庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin liber and liberare give liberty, liberal, liberate, liberation and deliver; the separate liber 'book' gives library and libretto.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 liber 与 liberare 衍生 liberty、liberal、liberate、liberation 与 deliver；另一个 liber「书」衍生 library 与 libretto。

items.example: The adjective described a free person, not a book.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述自由人，而非书。

items.example: The verb turned the state into an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把状态变成动作。

items.example: Liberation names the change, not the condition.
items.exampleCN: liberation 指变化，不指状态。

items.example: The unit liberated the town at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 部队在黎明解放了小镇。

items.example: The liberator refused a statue.
items.exampleCN: 这位解放者拒绝立像。

items.example: Liberty of speech has limits in law.
items.exampleCN: 言论自由在法律上有边界。

items.example: The word later became a political label.
items.exampleCN: 这个词后来成为政治标签。

items.example: The courier delivered the letter.
items.exampleCN: 信使投递了那封信。

items.example: The movement had a liberatory aim.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动带有解放目标。

latinEntries.structure: liber, libera, liberum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 解放；尤指法律上使脱离奴役或家长权；获得权利与自主
definition_en: the act of freeing someone from legal, social or personal control, especially from slavery or parental authority
core_image: 一份盖印的文件放在桌上，旁边是一条断开的锁链与一只张开的手
scene: 法庭的木桌上摆着一份盖印文书，书记员念出名字，站在栏杆外的人第一次以自己的名义签字。The emancipation of the enslaved workers, their legal release from ownership, changed the plantation economy.
sceneCN: 这里 emancipation 指「法律上使被奴役者获得自由」（第 1 个义项：以法律行为解除人身隶属）；句意为被奴役劳工的解放改变了种植园经济。可辨识物件：盖印文书、木桌、栏杆、签名笔、旁听席。

pos.zh: 解放；法律上的脱离隶属（可数，复数 emancipations）

senses.title: Legal freeing from slavery
senses.definition: the legal act by which an enslaved person ceases to be another's property
senses.definitionCN: 使被奴役者不再属于他人财产的法律行为
senses.example: The emancipation of the enslaved workers changed the plantation economy.
senses.exampleCN: 被奴役劳工的解放改变了种植园经济。
senses.why: e- 'out of' plus mancipare 'to transfer by hand' pictures a person taken out of the owner's hand.
senses.whyCN: e-「出」加 mancipare「以手转让」描绘一个人被从主人手中取出。

senses.title: A specific proclamation or decree
senses.definition: the named instrument by which a state declares a class of people free
senses.definitionCN: 国家宣布某一类人获得自由的具名文书
senses.example: Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in eighteen sixty-three.
senses.exampleCN: 林肯在一八六三年发布《解放宣言》。
senses.why: major legal acts receive titles, and the abstract noun becomes part of the title.
senses.whyCN: 重大法律行为获得标题，抽象名词便成为标题的一部分。

senses.title: Women's emancipation
senses.definition: the removal of legal, economic and social disabilities from women
senses.definitionCN: 解除女性在法律、经济与社会上的不利地位
senses.example: Women's emancipation reshaped inheritance and employment law.
senses.exampleCN: 妇女解放重塑了继承法与就业法。
senses.why: the legal image extends from slavery to any group held under guardianship.
senses.whyCN: 这一法律意象从奴隶制延伸到任何处于监护之下的群体。

senses.title: Legal release of a minor
senses.titleCN: 未成年人的法律脱离亲权
senses.definition: the ending of a parent's legal authority over a child before the usual age
senses.definitionCN: 在通常年龄之前终止父母对子女的法定支配权
senses.example: The court granted the teenager emancipation from her parents.
senses.exampleCN: 法院准许这名少女脱离父母监护。
senses.why: family law keeps the oldest technical sense: release from a household hand.
senses.whyCN: 家庭法保留了最古老的技术义：从家庭之手中释放。

senses.title: Intellectual or mental emancipation
senses.definition: release from prejudice, superstition or a belief that kept a mind dependent
senses.definitionCN: 从偏见、迷信或使心智依附的信念中解脱
senses.example: Reading Darwin was an intellectual emancipation for her.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读达尔文对她是一次思想解放。
senses.why: the hand that holds can be a habit as well as a person, so the word moves inward.
senses.whyCN: 握持的手既可以是人，也可以是习惯，因此这个词转向内在。

senses.title: A collective social process
senses.definition: the long movement by which a class or group gains rights and autonomy
senses.definitionCN: 某一阶级或群体逐步获得权利与自主的长期进程
senses.example: Emancipation was a process, not a single morning.
senses.exampleCN: 解放是一个过程，而不是某个早晨。
senses.why: when many people are freed over decades, the noun names the whole arc rather than one act.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人在数十年间陆续获释，这个名词就指整段弧线，而非单一行为。

senses.title: Abstraction: from dependence to autonomy
senses.definition: any shift by which a person or group moves from dependence to self-direction
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体从依附走向自主的任何转变
senses.example: The scholarship describes emancipation as the transfer of initiative.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把解放描述为主动权的转移。
senses.why: the core is a change of holder: the hand that decides moves to the person concerned.
senses.whyCN: 核心是持有者的改变：做决定的那只手移到当事人身上。

senses.title: Metaphor: formal removal of any constraint
senses.titleCN: 比喻：任何约束的正式解除
senses.definition: by extension, the formal ending of any binding condition, such as debt or contract
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何有约束力状态的正式终止，如债务或契约
senses.example: The bankruptcy ruling was an emancipation from old debt.
senses.exampleCN: 破产裁决是对旧债的一种「解放」。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the legal shape even when the master is a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 即使主人是账簿，这个比喻仍保留法律形态。

intro.en: Emancipation comes from Latin emancipare, e- 'out of' plus mancipare 'to transfer ownership', built on manus 'hand' and capere 'to take'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: emancipation 来自拉丁 emancipare，由 e-「出」与 mancipare「转让所有权」构成，后者基于 manus「手」与 capere「抓取」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manus meant 'hand' and capere 'to take'; a manceps was a person who took property in hand, an owner or purchaser.
items.cn: manus 意为「手」，capere 意为「抓取」；manceps 指把财产抓到手中的人，即所有者或购买者。

items.en: Mancipare meant 'to transfer ownership by the formal hand ritual', the legal sale of a thing or a person.
items.cn: mancipare 意为「通过正式的手势仪式转让所有权」，即对物或人的合法买卖。

items.en: E- 'out of' plus mancipare produced emancipare, 'to release a person from the hand of an owner or parent'.
items.cn: e-「出」加 mancipare 构成 emancipare，意为「把人从主人或父母之手中放出」。

items.en: Emancipatio named the legal act itself; Roman law used it for freeing a child from paternal power and for freeing a slave.
items.cn: emancipatio 指这一法律行为本身；罗马法用它表示使子女脱离父权，也用于释放奴隶。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries as a legal term; the antislavery sense became dominant from the late eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十六、十七世纪把这个词作为法律术语引入；从十八世纪末起，废奴义占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and deeper roots): dictionaries differ on the earliest English use, and the origins of both manus and capere are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与更深词根）：辞书对最早的英语用例说法不一，manus 与 capere 的来源均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds freeing words that are often confused with emancipation; group two holds the neighbouring ideas of autonomy.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 emancipation 混淆的释放类词；第二组是自主的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The formal freeing of a slave by an owner under Roman or older law; emancipation is the broader modern term.
entries.definitionCN: 指罗马法或更早法律下主人正式释放奴隶；emancipation 是更宽的现代说法。

entries.definition: To carry out emancipation; the noun names the act or process, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施解放；名词指行为或过程，动词指去做。

entries.definition: Describes a person who has been freed, often used for a minor or for a socially independent woman.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已获自由的人，常用于已脱离亲权的未成年人或社会独立的女性。

entries.definition: A handcuff, from Latin manica 'sleeve, glove'; it shares manus but names the restraint, not the release.
entries.definitionCN: 指手铐，来自拉丁 manica「袖子、手套」；同出 manus，但指束缚物，而非释放。

entries.definition: Release from control or confinement; it can be military or personal, while emancipation usually has a legal shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指脱离控制或拘禁；可军事、可个人，而 emancipation 通常带法律形态。

entries.definition: The condition of directing oneself; emancipation is the act of reaching it.
entries.definitionCN: 指自我支配的状态；emancipation 是达到它的行为。

entries.definition: The granting of a right, especially the vote; it is a specific legal emancipation, not the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指授予权利，尤指选举权；是一种具体的法律解放，而非总称。

entries.definition: The process of gaining confidence and capacity; it can occur without any legal change.
entries.definitionCN: 指获得信心与能力的过程；可以没有法律变化而发生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: manus plus capere, the Roman legal ritual and the real modern titles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：manus 加 capere、罗马法律仪式，以及真实的现代文献标题。

normal.en: manus 'hand' + capere 'take': an owner holds a person in hand.
normal.cn: manus「手」+ capere「抓」：主人把人抓在手里。

normal.en: e- 'out of' + mancipare: to take the person out of that hand.
normal.cn: e-「出」+ mancipare：把人从那只手里取出来。

normal.en: Roman law used it for a son leaving paternal power and for a slave leaving an owner.
normal.cn: 罗马法用它表示儿子脱离父权，也用于奴隶脱离主人。

normal.en: The family runs emancipate, emancipated, emancipation, emancipator, manumission, manacle.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 emancipate、emancipated、emancipation、emancipator、manumission、manacle。

normal.en: The Emancipation Proclamation is dated eighteen sixty-three.
normal.cn: 《解放宣言》定在一八六三年。

abstract.en: Picture a hand opening slowly, finger by finger, until it holds nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手一根手指、一根手指地慢慢张开，直到空无一物。

abstract.en: Picture a contract burned but the habit of obedience still warm.
abstract.cn: 想象契约烧掉了，服从的习惯却还有余温。

abstract.en: Picture a person signing a name that was never allowed before.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人签下此前从不被允许签的名字。

examples.en: Emancipation gave former slaves the right to marry and move freely.
examples.cn: 解放赋予前奴隶结婚与自由迁徙的权利。

examples.en: The court treated the inheritance as a step toward emancipation.
examples.cn: 法院把这份继承视为走向解放的一步。

examples.en: Her emancipation from family expectations took years.
examples.cn: 她摆脱家庭期待的过程花了多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）+ man（手）+ cip（拿）+ ation」——把人从主人手里拿出来 → 解放

root: 拉丁 emancipare = e-（出）+ mancipare（转让所有权），后者由 manus「手」+ capere「抓取」构成；名词 emancipatio。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one legal hand: a person is taken out of an owner's grip. That release becomes a named decree, a women's cause, a family-law act, an inner freedom, a long social arc, a shift of initiative and finally the formal end of any binding condition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一只法律之手展开：一个人被从主人的握持中取出。这次释放先成为具名法令，再成为妇女事业，再成为家庭法行为，再成为内在自由，再成为长期社会弧线，再成为主动权的转移，最后成为任何约束的正式终止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped paper beside a broken chain and an open hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份盖印文书，旁边一条断链与一只张开的手。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CORE: a hand releases, and a named paper records it.
branches.cn: 法律核心：一只手松开，一份具名文书记录下来。

branches.en: THE EXTENDED CLAIM: women and minors are released from older guardianship.
branches.cn: 延伸诉求：女性与未成年人从旧式监护中释放。

branches.en: THE INWARD AND THE LONG ARC: a mind can be freed, and a generation can be freed over time.
branches.cn: 向内与长弧：心智可被释放，一代人也可在时间中被释放。

branches.en: THE SHIFT OF INITIATIVE: the deciding hand moves to the person concerned.
branches.cn: 主动权的转移：做决定的手移到当事人身上。

branches.en: THE FORMAL END: even a ledger can play the master's part.
branches.cn: 正式终止：连账簿也能扮演主人的角色。

intro.en: Emancipation is a Latin legal compound that can be read hand by hand: a taking-out from a grip.
intro.cn: emancipation 是拉丁法律复合词，可以逐字读作「从握持中取出」。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual, manufacture and manacle; Latin capere gives capture, accept, receive and capacity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 manus 衍生 manual、manufacture 与 manacle；拉丁 capere 衍生 capture、accept、receive 与 capacity。

items.example: The prefix marks the movement out of a hold.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出离开握持的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the image of a grip.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「握持」的意象。

items.example: The root supplies the act of holding.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「握有」的动作。

items.example: The ritual put a thing into another's hand.
items.exampleCN: 这一仪式把物放进另一人的手中。

items.example: The verb pictured a release from power.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描绘从支配中释放。

items.meaning: a release from ownership or power
items.example: Emancipation changed the legal status of a person.
items.exampleCN: 解放改变了一个人的法律地位。

items.example: The state emancipated the apprentices.
items.exampleCN: 国家解放了这些学徒。

items.example: The emancipated workers signed their own contracts.
items.exampleCN: 获释的工人自己签合同。

items.example: The emancipator avoided the word hero.
items.exampleCN: 这位解放者避开了「英雄」一词。

items.meaning: the formal freeing of a slave
items.example: Manumission was the older legal ritual.
