definition_zh: 废除；尤指废除奴隶制；取消某项制度、法律或做法
definition_en: the formal ending of a system, law or practice, especially slavery
core_image: 一本旧法令被合上，封皮上的印章被划去，旁边是一截断裂的锁链
scene: 议事厅里，议员们把一叠旧法令搬到一边，书记在末页写下终止二字，旁听席上有人低声哭泣。The abolition of the slave trade, its formal ending by law, forced merchants to rebuild their business.
sceneCN: 这里 abolition 指「正式废除一项制度」（第 1 个义项：以法律手段终止奴隶制一类制度）；句意为奴隶贸易的废除迫使商人重建自己的生意。可辨识物件：旧法令、印章、断裂锁链、议事厅长桌、旁听席。

pos.zh: 废除；废止（可数，复数 abolitions）

collocations.phrase: the abolition of the slave trade

derivatives.zh: 废奴主义者；主张废除者

senses.title: The formal ending of slavery
senses.definition: the legal termination of slavery as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 以法律终止奴隶制这一制度
senses.example: The abolition of the slave trade forced merchants to rebuild their business.
senses.exampleCN: 奴隶贸易的废除迫使商人重建自己的生意。
senses.why: abolere is 'to do away with, efface'; the noun names the act of making an institution cease to exist.
senses.whyCN: abolere 是「取消、抹去」；名词指使一项制度不复存在的行为。

senses.title: The abolition movement
senses.definition: the organised campaign that sought to end slavery and the slave trade
senses.definitionCN: 争取结束奴隶制与奴隶贸易的组织化运动
senses.example: Abolition grew from pamphlets into a mass campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 废奴运动从小册子发展成群众运动。
senses.why: a cause takes the name of its goal, so the abstract noun also labels the movement.
senses.whyCN: 事业以目标为名，因此这个抽象名词也标示运动。

senses.title: Repeal of a law or practice
senses.definition: the ending of a statute, rule or custom by the authority that made it
senses.definitionCN: 由制定机关终止一项法规、规则或惯例
senses.example: The abolition of the old tariff raised prices for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 旧关税的废除使价格升了一年。
senses.why: the word is not tied to slavery; any institution can be abolished, from a tax to a monarch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不限于奴隶制；任何制度都可被废除，从税收到君主制。

senses.title: The repealing statute itself
senses.definition: the named act or instrument that declares an institution at an end
senses.definitionCN: 宣布某项制度终止的具名法案或文书
senses.example: The abolition act named a date for the change.
senses.exampleCN: 废除法案为这一变化指定了日期。
senses.why: legal English names the instrument by the result it produces, as with abolition.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语用结果来命名工具，abolition 就是如此。

senses.title: Gradual or partial abolition
senses.definition: the ending of one part of an institution before the rest, such as the trade before the institution
senses.definitionCN: 先终止制度的某一部分，再终止其余，如先废贸易再废制度
senses.example: Gradual abolition left a loophole for another decade.
senses.exampleCN: 逐步废除留下了另一个十年的漏洞。
senses.why: reform often moves by stages, so the noun takes modifiers such as gradual and partial.
senses.whyCN: 改革常分阶段推进，因此这个名词可带「逐步」「部分」等修饰语。

senses.title: International abolition
senses.definition: a worldwide agreement or norm ending a practice such as the death penalty or a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 终止死刑或某类武器等做法的全球性协定或规范
senses.example: International abolition of the trade required many treaties.
senses.exampleCN: 这一贸易的国际废除需要许多条约。
senses.why: some practices can only end across borders, so the noun gains a global scale.
senses.whyCN: 有些做法只能跨国终止，因此这个名词获得全球尺度。

senses.title: Abstraction: complete cancellation
senses.definition: any complete cancellation of a rule, custom or category, not only a legal one
senses.definitionCN: 任何对规则、惯例或类别的彻底取消，不限于法律
senses.example: The abolition of the weekly meeting surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 每周例会的取消让所有人意外。
senses.why: the core sense needs only a thing that exists and an authority that ends it.
senses.whyCN: 核心义只需要一物存在，以及一个权威将其终止。

senses.title: Metaphor: institutional disappearance
senses.definition: the disappearance of a structure so completely that later users no longer notice its absence
senses.definitionCN: 某一结构彻底消失，以致后来者不再察觉其缺失
senses.example: The abolition of that custom is visible only in old photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 那种习俗的废除只能从老照片里看出来。
senses.why: the deepest sense is erasure: not reform but the removal of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是抹除：不是改良，而是把事物本身移走。

intro.en: Abolition comes from Latin abolere 'to destroy, efface', through French. Its deeper formation is debated. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: abolition 经法语来自拉丁 abolere「摧毁、抹去」，其更深构词存在争论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Abolere meant 'to destroy, efface, cause to die out'; it is generally analysed as ab- 'away' plus olere 'to grow'.
items.cn: abolere 意为「摧毁、抹去、使消亡」；一般认为由 ab-「离开」加 olere「生长」构成。

items.en: Olere 'to grow' is related to alere 'to nourish'; the connection is generally accepted, while the deeper root remains uncertain and reconstructed.
items.cn: olere「生长」与 alere「滋养」相关；这一联系一般被接受，而其更深词根仍不确定，属重构。

items.en: Old French abolir carried the verb into English as abolish, and the noun abolition followed from the Latin action noun.
items.cn: 古法语 abolir 把动词带入英语作 abolish，名词 abolition 则来自拉丁行为名词。

items.en: Abolition entered English in the seventeenth century as a general word for doing away with something.
items.cn: abolition 在十七世纪进入英语，泛指取消某物。

items.en: From the late eighteenth century the word became the standard label for ending the slave trade and then slavery itself.
items.cn: 从十八世纪末起，这个词成为结束奴隶贸易、继而结束奴隶制本身的标准标签。

items.en: Source uncertain (the olere analysis): some dictionaries treat the ab- plus olere division as probable rather than certain, and the pre-Latin root of olere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（olere 的分析）：一些辞书把 ab- 加 olere 的划分视为「很可能」而非确定，olere 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds abolish-family words that are easily confused with abolition; group two holds the neighbouring ideas of ending a rule.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 abolition 混淆的废除类词；第二组是终止规则的邻近概念。

entries.definition: To end an institution by authority; the noun names the act, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指由权威终止制度；名词指行为，动词指去做。

entries.definition: One who campaigns for abolition; it names the supporter, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指为废奴而奔走的人；命名支持者，而非行为。

entries.definition: A rarer noun for the same act; abolition is the established form in legal and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一行为的较少见名词；abolition 是法律与历史写作中的通行形式。

entries.definition: Describing something that tends to abolish; it cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述有废除倾向的事物；不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The formal cancellation of a law by the body that made it; narrower than abolition, which can end an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指由制定机关正式取消一项法律；比 abolition 窄，后者可终止整个制度。

entries.definition: A declaration that something never had legal force, such as a marriage or contract; it looks backward, not forward.
entries.definitionCN: 指宣布某事物自始无效，如婚姻或合同；它向后看，而非向前。

entries.definition: The withdrawal of a licence, right or promise; it removes a permission rather than an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指撤回许可、权利或承诺；移走的是许可，而非制度。

entries.definition: The freeing of persons from slavery or control; abolition ends the institution, emancipation changes the persons' status.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人脱离奴役或控制；abolition 终止制度，emancipation 改变人的身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the French verb, the antislavery campaign and the real legal compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：那个法语动词、废奴运动，以及真实的法条组合。

normal.en: ab- 'away' + olere 'grow': to cause something to grow away until it is gone.
normal.cn: ab-「离开」+ olere「生长」：使某物长到消失。

normal.en: The verb is abolish; the noun is abolition; the person is an abolitionist.
normal.cn: 动词是 abolish，名词是 abolition，人是 abolitionist。

normal.en: The family runs abolish, abolition, abolitionist, abolitionism, abolishable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 abolish、abolition、abolitionist、abolitionism、abolishable。

normal.en: The cause is dated to the late eighteenth century, when the slave trade was attacked first.
normal.cn: 这场事业定在十八世纪末，最先受攻击的是奴隶贸易。

normal.en: Typical partners are slavery, slave trade, capital punishment, gradual.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是奴隶制、奴隶贸易、死刑与「逐步」。

abstract.en: Picture a word removed from a dictionary so that later readers never meet it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词被从词典里移除，后来的读者再也遇不到它。

abstract.en: Picture a road erased and grass growing where the traffic used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路被抹去，旧日车流处长出草。

abstract.en: Picture a chair taken out of a room; the space remains, but nothing fills it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子被搬出房间；空间还在，却空无一物。

examples.en: Abolition was achieved only after decades of petitioning.
examples.cn: 经过数十年的请愿，废除才得以实现。

examples.en: The abolition of that tax changed how the port was funded.
examples.cn: 那项税的废除改变了港口的资金来源。

examples.en: Historians debate whether abolition helped the workers it was meant to save.
examples.cn: 历史学家争论废奴是否帮助了它本应拯救的工人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ab（离开）+ olish（完成）」——让制度离开并做到底 → 废除

root: 拉丁 abolere「摧毁、抹去」，一般认为由 ab-（离开）+ olere（生长）构成；olere 与 alere「滋养」相关，更深词根属重构。名词 abolitio 经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one erasure: an authority makes an institution cease to exist. The erasure becomes slavery's ending, a movement, a repealed statute, the act itself, staged reform, a global norm, any cancellation and finally a disappearance no longer noticed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次抹除展开：权威使一项制度不再存在。这次抹除先成为奴隶制的终结，再成为运动、被废的法令、法令本身、分阶段改革、全球规范、任何取消，最后成为不再被察觉的消失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old statute closed, its seal struck through, a broken chain beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本旧法令被合上，印章被划去，旁边一截断链。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION AND THE CAUSE: ending slavery and the campaign that demanded it share one word.
branches.cn: 制度与事业：终止奴隶制与要求它的运动共用一个词。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE PAPER: a practice ends, and an act records the ending.
branches.cn: 规则与纸面：惯例终止，法案记录这次终止。

branches.en: THE STAGES: reform can be gradual at home and global abroad.
branches.cn: 阶段：改革可在国内逐步，也可在国际上铺开。

branches.en: ANY CANCELLATION: a meeting, a tax or a category can be abolished.
branches.cn: 任何取消：会议、税项或类别都可被废除。

branches.en: THE ERASURE: the deepest sense is a structure gone so fully that its absence is invisible.
branches.cn: 抹除：最深的一层是结构彻底消失，连缺失都看不见。

intro.en: Abolition is a Latin verb turned noun, carried through French, with a root that also underlies words about growth.
intro.cn: abolition 是由拉丁动词转成的名词，经法语进入英语，其词根也构成若干表示「生长」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin abolere gives abolish and abolition; the related olere and alere line gives adult and adolescent, where growth is literal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 abolere 衍生 abolish 与 abolition；相关的 olere 与 alere 一线衍生 adult 与 adolescent，那里的「生长」仍是字面的。

items.example: The prefix marks removal from existence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出「从存在中移除」。

items.example: The root contributes the image of growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「生长」的意象。

items.meaning: to cause to grow away, destroy
items.example: The verb pictured a thing wasting away to nothing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描绘事物消退至无。

items.example: Parliament abolished the duty.
items.exampleCN: 议会废除了这项税。

items.example: Abolition required a new constitution.
items.exampleCN: 废除需要一部新宪法。

items.example: The abolitionist printed a weekly paper.
items.exampleCN: 这位废奴主义者印行一份周报。

items.meaningCN: 主张废除奴隶制的主义
items.example: Abolitionism spread through the ports.
items.exampleCN: 废奴主义在港口传播。

items.example: Not every custom is abolishable by law.
items.exampleCN: 并非每种习俗都能由法律废除。

items.structure: adult (Latin adultus, grown up, from adolescere)
items.example: The word shares the growth image, not the abolition sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词共享「生长」意象，但不含废除义。

definition_zh: 废奴主义者；主张废除某项制度的人；形容词：废奴主义的
definition_en: a person who campaigns for the abolition of slavery or another institution; also the adjective describing such a position
core_image: 印刷机旁堆着刚印好的小册子，墙上钉着请愿名单，一只手正把传单递给路人
scene: 街角的小印刷铺里，油墨未干的小册子摞在木箱上，几个人把传单塞给过路人，墙上贴满请愿名单。The abolitionist, a campaigner for ending slavery, printed a thousand pamphlets before the debate.
sceneCN: 这里 abolitionist 指「主张废除奴隶制的活动者」（第 1 个义项：为废奴而行动的人）；句意为这位废奴主义者在辩论前印了一千份小册子。可辨识物件：印刷机、小册子、木箱、请愿名单、递出的传单。

pos.zh: 废奴主义者；主张废除某项制度的人（可数，复数 abolitionists）
废奴主义的；主张废除的（作定语，如 abolitionist press）

senses.title: A campaigner against slavery
senses.definition: a person who worked to end slavery and the slave trade
senses.definitionCN: 为结束奴隶制与奴隶贸易而奔走的人
senses.example: The abolitionist printed a thousand pamphlets before the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 这位废奴主义者在辩论前印了一千份小册子。
senses.why: abolition plus -ist names the person who seeks the ending of an institution, and the first institution in question was slavery.
senses.whyCN: abolition 加 -ist 命名争取终止制度的人，而当时首先针对的制度就是奴隶制。

senses.title: A member of an organised movement
senses.definition: someone belonging to a society, party or network dedicated to abolition
senses.definitionCN: 隶属于致力于废除的协会、党派或网络的人
senses.example: Abolitionists met every Tuesday in the back room.
senses.exampleCN: 废奴主义者每周二在后屋聚会。
senses.why: a cause that organizes turns supporters into members, and the agent noun marks that role.
senses.whyCN: 组织起来的事业把支持者变成成员，施动名词标示这一角色。

senses.title: An advocate of ending any institution
senses.titleCN: 主张废除任何制度的人
senses.definition: by extension, a person who campaigns to end a practice such as a tax, a prison system or a monarchy
senses.definitionCN: 引申指为终止某项做法而奔走的人，如某项税、监狱制度或君主制
senses.example: Prison abolitionists borrowed the word from the antislavery struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 监狱废除论者从反奴隶制斗争中借用了这个词。
senses.why: the suffix is productive: any institution can gain an -ist who wants it gone.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀能产：任何制度都能得到一个想让它消失的 -ist。

senses.title: A supporter of an abolitionist organ
senses.titleCN: 废奴主义报刊或组织的支持者
senses.definition: a reader, funder or writer attached to an abolitionist newspaper or society
senses.definitionCN: 与废奴报刊或协会相关的读者、资助者或撰稿人
senses.example: The paper's abolitionists raised money for the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸的废奴主义支持者为印刷机筹款。
senses.why: movements need infrastructure, and the noun also labels those who sustain it.
senses.whyCN: 运动需要基础设施，这个名词也标示维持它的人。

senses.title: A historical type
senses.definition: the recognised nineteenth-century figure studied in histories of the Atlantic slave trade
senses.definitionCN: 大西洋奴隶贸易史研究中公认的十九世纪人物类型
senses.example: Historians compare British and American abolitionists.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家比较英国与美国的废奴主义者。
senses.why: when a movement becomes history, its members become a social type with shared tactics and vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 当运动成为历史，其成员就成为具有共同策略与语汇的社会类型。

senses.title: The adjective use
senses.definition: describing a newspaper, society, argument or position as belonging to abolitionism
senses.definitionCN: 描述报纸、协会、论点或立场属于废奴主义
senses.example: The abolitionist press reached readers in three states.
senses.exampleCN: 废奴主义报刊的读者遍及三个州。
senses.why: English often lets agent nouns work as modifiers without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让施动名词不加变化地充当修饰语。

senses.title: By extension: one who urges cancellation
senses.titleCN: 比喻：主张取消某项做法的人
senses.definition: a person who argues that a practice should be scrapped rather than reformed
senses.definitionCN: 主张某项做法应被取消而非改良的人
senses.example: The manager became an abolitionist about the weekly report.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理成了每周报告的「废除派」。
senses.why: the metaphor contrasts abolition with reform: one ends the thing, the other repairs it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把「废除」与「改良」对照：一个终止事物，一个修补事物。

senses.title: Abstraction: an advocate of erasure
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：主张抹除制度的人
senses.definition: anyone who seeks the complete removal of a structure rather than its adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 任何寻求彻底移除某一结构而非调整它的人
senses.example: An abolitionist is a reformer who refuses to keep the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 废奴主义者是拒绝保留框架的改革者。
senses.why: the deepest sense is a stance toward institutions: not improve them but end them.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是对制度的态度：不是改良，而是终结。

intro.en: Abolitionist is an English formation from abolition plus the agent suffix -ist, though a French parallel exists. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: abolitionist 是英语由 abolition 加施动后缀 -ist 构成，法语中也有平行形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: The word is built inside English from abolition and the agent suffix -ist, which marks a person devoted to a cause.
items.cn: 这个词在英语内部由 abolition 与施动后缀 -ist 构成，后者标示投身某项事业的人。

items.en: French abolitionniste is a close parallel formed at about the same time; whether English borrowed it or coined its own is not settled.
items.cn: 法语 abolitionniste 是大约同时形成的平行词；英语是借用还是自造，尚无定论。

items.en: The suffix goes back through Latin -ista to Greek -istēs, an agent ending used for adherents of a practice or school.
items.cn: 这个后缀经拉丁 -ista 上溯希腊 -istēs，是用来指某种实践或学派追随者的施动词尾。

items.en: The word is recorded in the 1780s and 1790s, when campaigns against the slave trade were organizing in Britain and France.
items.cn: 这个词见于十八世纪八九十年代，当时英法的反奴隶贸易运动正在组织起来。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the term was extended to campaigns against other institutions, such as capital punishment.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，这个词被扩展到反对其他制度的运动，如废除死刑。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation and borrowing path): dictionaries do not agree on the earliest use, and the French-or-English origin of the English word remains open.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与借入路径）：辞书对最早用例说法不一，英语词究竟源自法语还是英语自造仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds abolition-family words easily confused with the person noun; group two holds neighbouring roles in reform.
note.cn: 第一组是易与这个人物名词混淆的废除类词；第二组是改革中的邻近角色。

entries.definition: The ending of an institution; an abolitionist is the person who seeks that ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指终止制度的行为；abolitionist 是寻求这一终止的人。

entries.definition: The body of belief and activity behind abolition; the -ist is one adherent of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指废除背后的信念与活动体系；-ist 是其中一名追随者。

entries.definition: One who seeks the freeing of enslaved people; abolitionists sought to end the institution itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻求使被奴役者获自由的人；废奴主义者则寻求终止制度本身。

entries.definition: Describing measures that abolish; it is not a noun for a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述具有废除作用的措施；不是指人的名词。

entries.definition: Anyone who campaigns for change; abolitionist specifies the change sought.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何为改变而奔走的人；abolitionist 具体说明所寻求的改变。

entries.definition: A person who runs a sustained public effort; the word names the activity, not the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 指开展持续公共行动的人；这个词命名活动，而非目标。

entries.definition: Opposed to slavery; it can describe a newspaper or a voter without naming a profession of activism.
entries.definitionCN: 指反对奴隶制的；可描述报纸或选民，而不指职业活动者。

entries.definition: One who seeks to improve an institution; an abolitionist wants it ended instead.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻求改良制度的人；废奴主义者则要终止它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the base noun, the agent suffix and the historical campaign.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：基础名词、施动后缀与历史运动。

normal.en: abolition + -ist: the person who works for the ending.
normal.cn: abolition + -ist：为终止而努力的人。

normal.en: -ist goes back to Greek -istēs, a person attached to a practice or school.
normal.cn: -ist 上溯希腊 -istēs，指依附某种实践或学派的人。

normal.en: The family runs abolish, abolition, abolitionism, abolitionist, abolitionary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 abolish、abolition、abolitionism、abolitionist、abolitionary。

normal.en: The campaign is dated to the 1780s and 1790s, against the slave trade first.
normal.cn: 这场运动定在十八世纪八九十年代，最先针对奴隶贸易。

normal.en: The word also works as an adjective: abolitionist press, abolitionist society.
normal.cn: 这个词也作形容词：废奴主义报刊、废奴协会。

abstract.en: Picture a person handing out a pamphlet at a harbour gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在港口门口散发小册子。

abstract.en: Picture a name added to a petition until the page is full.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被添上请愿书，直到纸页写满。

abstract.en: Picture a reformer who brings a hammer, not a needle.
abstract.cn: 想象一位改革者带来的是锤子，而不是针线。

examples.en: The abolitionist argued that free labour was also more productive.
examples.cn: 这位废奴主义者主张自由劳动也更有生产力。

examples.en: Abolitionists faced violence in several port cities.
examples.cn: 废奴主义者在若干港口城市遭遇暴力。

examples.en: The exhibition honours an abolitionist who has been largely forgotten.
examples.cn: 展览纪念一位基本被遗忘的废奴主义者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「abolition（废除）+ ist（人）」——主张把制度废掉的人 → 废奴主义者

root: 由英语 abolition 加施动后缀 -ist 构成；-ist 经拉丁 -ista 上溯希腊 -istēs。abolition 来自拉丁 abolere「抹去」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from the person who fought slavery, through the movement member and the extended campaigner, to the supporter of a press, the historical type, the adjective, and finally the general advocate of cancellation and of erasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从反对奴隶制的人出发，经过运动成员与扩展的活动者，再到报刊支持者、历史类型、形容词用法，最后落到一般主张取消者与主张抹除者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: inky pamphlets stacked by a press, a petition on the wall and a leaflet held out to a stranger.
core.cn: 核心意象：印刷机旁堆着油墨未干的小册子，墙上是请愿书，一只手把传单递给陌生人。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE BODY: an individual campaigner and an organised member share the name.
branches.cn: 个人与团体：个体活动者与组织成员共用这个名称。

branches.en: THE EXTENDED CAUSE: any practice can find its own abolitionist.
branches.cn: 扩展的事业：任何做法都能找到自己的废除派。

branches.en: THE INFRASTRUCTURE AND THE RECORD: a press needs supporters, and history turns them into a type.
branches.cn: 设施与记录：报刊需要支持者，历史把他们变成类型。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: the same form works as an adjective before a noun.
branches.cn: 修饰语：同一形式可在名词前作形容词。

branches.en: THE STANCE: the deepest sense is a refusal to keep the frame.
branches.cn: 立场：最深的一层是拒绝保留框架。

intro.en: Abolitionist is a transparent derivative: a Latin-derived base noun plus a Greek-derived agent suffix.
intro.cn: abolitionist 是透明的派生词：拉丁来源的基础名词加希腊来源的施动后缀。

latinIntro.en: The base abolition goes back to Latin abolere and abolitio; the suffix -ist reaches English through Latin -ista from Greek -istēs.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 abolition 上溯拉丁 abolere 与 abolitio；后缀 -ist 经拉丁 -ista 从希腊 -istēs 进入英语。

items.example: The Latin verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: The noun supplied the English base abolition.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供英语基础词 abolition。

items.example: Abolition was the goal of the campaign.
items.exampleCN: 废除是这场运动的目标。

items.meaning: a person devoted to a cause
items.example: The suffix marks adherence, not mere knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标示投身，而非仅仅了解。

items.example: The abolitionist spoke at the quay.
items.exampleCN: 这位废奴主义者在水码头演讲。

items.example: Abolitionism grew in the port towns.
items.exampleCN: 废奴主义在港口城镇成长。

items.example: The abolitionary law passed narrowly.
items.exampleCN: 这项废除法案以微弱多数通过。

items.structure: abolish (from French abolir, from Latin abolere)
items.example: They voted to abolish the duty.
items.exampleCN: 他们投票废除这项税。

items.meaning: one who seeks the freeing of people
items.example: An emancipationist stressed immediate freedom.
items.exampleCN: 一位解放论者强调立即自由。

definition_zh: 考古遗址；保存有古代人类活动遗存并被研究的地点；发掘现场
definition_en: a place where the material remains of past human activity are preserved and studied
core_image: 黄土剖面上露出半截陶罐与石墙基，标尺和刷子放在一旁的托盘里
scene: 荒野的土坡被切开一条整齐的探沟，剖面里露出陶片与墙基，工作人员蹲在网格旁记录编号。The archaeology site, a place holding ancient remains, yielded pottery that dated the settlement to the Bronze Age.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeology site 指「保存有古代遗存并被研究的地点」（第 1 个义项：具有考古价值的具体地点）；句意为这处考古遗址出土的陶器把聚落年代定在青铜时代。可辨识物件：土坡剖面、探沟、陶片、石墙基、记录网格。

pos.zh: 考古遗址；考古地点（可数，复数 archaeology sites）

senses.title: A place with archaeological remains
senses.definition: a location that holds material traces of past human activity and is studied as such
senses.definitionCN: 保存过去人类活动物质痕迹并作为研究对象的地点
senses.example: The archaeology site yielded pottery that dated the settlement to the Bronze Age.
senses.exampleCN: 这处考古遗址出土的陶器把聚落年代定在青铜时代。
senses.why: archaeology names the study and site names the place, so the phrase is the place where that study works.
senses.whyCN: archaeology 指研究，site 指地点，因此短语就是这门研究作业的地点。

senses.title: An active excavation site
senses.definition: a place currently being dug, recorded and sampled by a team
senses.definitionCN: 正由团队挖掘、记录与取样的地点
senses.example: The archaeology site was closed to visitors during the dig.
senses.exampleCN: 发掘期间，考古现场不对游客开放。
senses.why: a site becomes active when tools arrive, and the phrase then names a workplace rather than a dot on a map.
senses.whyCN: 工具一到，遗址就成为活动场所，此时短语指工作现场而非地图上的一个点。

senses.title: A protected or managed site
senses.definition: a place legally protected, fenced or maintained for preservation and public interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 依法保护、围护或维护以供保存与公众解读的地点
senses.example: The archaeology site is managed by the regional museum.
senses.exampleCN: 这处考古遗址由地区博物馆管理。
senses.why: once a place is valued, it acquires rules, staff and boundaries, and the phrase takes on administration.
senses.whyCN: 一旦地点被珍视，它就有了规则、人员与边界，短语也随之带行政管理色彩。

senses.title: A type of site
senses.definition: a category such as settlement, tomb, city, kiln or workshop
senses.definitionCN: 聚落、墓葬、城址、窑址或作坊等类别
senses.example: Each archaeology site type leaves a different pattern in the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 每一类考古遗址在土壤中留下不同的图案。
senses.why: archaeologists classify places by function, and the phrase can name the class as well as the instance.
senses.whyCN: 考古学家按功能给地点分类，这个短语既可指实例，也可指类别。

senses.title: A registered or listed site
senses.definition: a place entered in an official inventory with a number and a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 以编号与边界录入官方名录的地点
senses.example: The archaeology site appears on the national register.
senses.exampleCN: 这处考古遗址见于国家名录。
senses.why: modern heritage practice turns places into records, and the phrase follows them into the archive.
senses.whyCN: 现代遗产实践把地点变成记录，短语也随之进入档案。

senses.title: An underwater or underground site
senses.definition: a place of remains preserved beneath water, sediment or later construction
senses.definitionCN: 遗存保存在水下、沉积物下或后期建筑之下的地点
senses.example: Divers mapped an archaeology site beneath the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员绘制了港湾水下的考古遗址。
senses.why: the same definition applies wherever the layers lie, so the phrase extends below the surface.
senses.whyCN: 无论地层在哪里，定义都适用，因此短语延伸到地表之下。

senses.title: Metaphor: a layered place of memory
senses.titleCN: 比喻：层层叠压的记忆之地
senses.definition: by extension, any place where earlier lives remain visible under later ones
senses.definitionCN: 引申指早期生活仍能在后期痕迹下看见的任何地点
senses.example: The old quarter is an archaeology site of the city's habits.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区是这座城市生活习惯的「考古遗址」。
senses.why: the metaphor uses stratigraphy: each generation leaves a layer that the next covers.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻使用地层学：每一代人留下一层，下一代将其覆盖。

senses.title: Abstraction: a readable field of traces
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：可解读的痕迹场
senses.definition: any bounded field of traces that can be read as evidence of a past order
senses.definitionCN: 任何可被解读为过去秩序证据的有界痕迹场
senses.example: A trial is an archaeology site of decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 一场审判是决策的「考古遗址」。
senses.why: the deepest sense removes the soil: what matters is that traces survive in order and can be read.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层抽掉了泥土：重要的是痕迹有序留存并可被解读。

intro.en: Archaeology joins Greek arkhaios 'ancient' to -logia 'study'; site comes from Latin situs 'place'. The phrase is a modern English combination. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: archaeology 把希腊 arkhaios「古老的」与 -logia「学问」结合；site 来自拉丁 situs「地点」。短语是近代英语组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arkhaios meant 'ancient, from the beginning', built on arkhē 'beginning, first place'; the deeper origin of arkhē is debated.
items.cn: arkhaios 意为「古老的、自起初的」，由 arkhē「开端、首位」构成；arkhē 的更深来源有争论。

items.en: Arkhaiologia meant 'the study or telling of ancient things'; it joined arkhaios to -logia, from logos 'account, reason'.
items.cn: arkhaiologia 意为「对古老事物的研究或讲述」；它把 arkhaios 与 -logia 结合，后者来自 logos「叙述、理性」。

items.en: The Latinized form archaeologia entered European scholarly language in the seventeenth century, and English archaeology followed.
items.cn: 拉丁化形式 archaeologia 在十七世纪进入欧洲学术语言，英语 archaeology 随之而来。

items.en: Situs meant 'a place, position, situation', from sinere 'to let, set down'; its past participle situs also gave the English adjective site-related forms.
items.cn: situs 意为「地点、位置、处境」，来自 sinere「放置、允许」；其过去分词 situs 也衍生英语中与 site 相关的形式。

items.en: Archaeology site is a modern English phrase; the more usual form in professional writing is archaeological site, and both are current.
items.cn: archaeology site 是近代英语短语；专业写作中更常见的形式是 archaeological site，两者都在使用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation and root shapes): no dictionary fixes the first use of the exact phrase, the origin of arkhē is debated, and the pre-Latin root of sinere is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根形态）：没有辞书确定这一确切短语的首次使用；arkhē 的来源有争论，sinere 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds site and archaeology words constantly confused with the phrase; group two holds neighbouring heritage ideas.
note.cn: 第一组是常与该短语混淆的 site 与 archaeology 类词；第二组是遗产领域的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The standard adjective-plus-noun wording; archaeology site is an abbreviated variant used in some writing.
entries.definitionCN: 标准形容词加名词说法；archaeology site 是某些写作中的简略变体。

entries.definition: The study of past human activity through material remains; it names the field, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过物质遗存研究过去人类活动的学科；命名领域，不指地点。

entries.definition: A practitioner of archaeology; a site is where that practitioner works.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事考古学的人；遗址是其工作地点。

entries.definition: A place currently being dug; an archaeology site may be protected and unexcavated.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在被挖掘的地点；考古遗址可能受保护且尚未发掘。

entries.definition: The standing or fallen remains of a structure; a site can be ruinous or buried and invisible.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑物的残存或倒塌部分；遗址可以是有残迹的，也可以完全埋在地下。

entries.definition: A structure built to commemorate or preserve memory; it may be part of a site but is not the site itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指为纪念或保存记忆而建的构筑物；它可能是遗址的一部分，但不等于遗址。

entries.definition: A place recognised for cultural or natural value; the label comes from preservation policy rather than from research.
entries.definitionCN: 指因文化或自然价值而受认可的地点；这一标签来自保护政策，而非研究。

entries.definition: An excavation, especially in informal speech; it names the work, not the place.
entries.definitionCN: 指发掘，尤用于口语；命名工作，而非地点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek roots, the Latin word for place and the stratigraphic picture.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊词根、拉丁语「地点」一词，以及地层剖面图。

normal.en: arkhaios 'ancient' + -logia 'study': the study of ancient things.
normal.cn: arkhaios「古老」+ -logia「学问」：对古老事物的研究。

normal.en: site is from Latin situs, a place set down.
normal.cn: site 来自拉丁 situs，指被放置下来的地点。

normal.en: The family runs archaeology, archaeological, archaeologist, site, situate, situation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 archaeology、archaeological、archaeologist、site、situate、situation。

normal.en: A site is read in layers: the lowest layer is usually the oldest.
normal.cn: 遗址按层解读：最下面的层通常最古老。

normal.en: The usual professional wording is archaeological site.
normal.cn: 专业写作中通行的说法是 archaeological site。

abstract.en: Picture a page of earth where each generation wrote one line over the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一页泥土，每一代人在上一行之上写一行。

abstract.en: Picture a city whose older streets still shape the newer ones above them.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，旧街道仍在塑造其上的新街道。

abstract.en: Picture a room where furniture was moved but the dents in the floor remain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，家具搬走了，地板上的凹痕还在。

examples.en: The archaeology site was fenced before the road was widened.
examples.cn: 在道路拓宽之前，这处考古遗址被围护起来。

examples.en: Students mapped the archaeology site with a simple grid.
examples.cn: 学生们用简单网格绘制了这处考古遗址。

examples.en: A single pottery shard can date an archaeology site.
examples.cn: 一片陶片就能确定一处考古遗址的年代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「archaeology（考古）+ site（地点）」——考古学家工作的那片地点 → 考古遗址

root: archaeology 来自希腊 arkhaiologia = arkhaios「古老的」+ -logia「学问」，arkhē 为「开端」；site 来自拉丁 situs「地点」，源于 sinere「放置」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from a place holding remains, through the active dig and the managed and classified site, to the registered, underwater and buried place, then to a layered metaphor and finally to any readable field of traces.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从保存遗存的地点出发，经过活动中的发掘现场、受管理与分类的遗址，再到登记、水下与埋藏的地点，再到层叠比喻，最后落到任何可解读的痕迹场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut slope showing a broken jar and a stone footing, with a ruler and brush on a tray.
core.cn: 核心意象：切开的土坡露出破陶罐与石墙基，托盘上放着标尺与刷子。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND THE WORK: a dot on the map becomes a workplace when the tools arrive.
branches.cn: 地点与工作：地图上的一个点在工具到来时变成工作现场。

branches.en: CARE AND CATEGORY: protection gives boundaries, function gives types.
branches.cn: 照管与类别：保护给出边界，功能给出类型。

branches.en: THE RECORD AND THE DEPTH: registers name places, and layers hide them.
branches.cn: 记录与深度：名录给地点命名，地层把它们藏起。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any old quarter can be read as stratified memory.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何老城区都可读作层叠的记忆。

branches.en: TRACES WITHOUT SOIL: the deepest sense is ordered evidence that can be read.
branches.cn: 无土的痕迹：最深的一层是有序、可解读的证据。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Greek-derived discipline word with a Latin-derived place word, so both halves are readable.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的学科词与拉丁来源的地点词结合，两部分都可读。

latinIntro.en: Greek arkhaios and logos give archaeology and archaeological; Latin situs and sinere give site, situate and situation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 arkhaios 与 logos 衍生 archaeology 与 archaeological；拉丁 situs 与 sinere 衍生 site、situate 与 situation。

items.example: The prefix marks the age of the material.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出材料的古老。

items.example: The suffix turns a subject into a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把主题变成学科。

items.example: Archaeology reads objects as evidence.
items.exampleCN: 考古学把物件读作证据。

items.example: The report used the archaeological record.
items.exampleCN: 报告使用了考古记录。

items.example: The archaeologist brushed the surface.
items.exampleCN: 考古学家刷去表面。

items.example: The site lay beside a dry stream.
items.exampleCN: 这处地点在一条干涸小溪旁。

items.example: The Latin noun supplied the English word site.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词提供英语 site。

items.example: The village was situated above the flood line.
items.exampleCN: 村庄位于洪水线之上。

items.meaning: a position or set of circumstances
items.example: The word also means a state of affairs.
items.exampleCN: 这个词也指事态。

latinEntries.structure: archaeologia, archaeologiae (f., first declension; from Greek)

definition_zh: 发掘；考古发掘工作、现场或成果；土方开挖；挖出的坑
definition_en: the process of digging out earth or buried material, especially for archaeology, or the hole made by digging
core_image: 方形探坑一层层向下收窄，坑壁插着标签，坑底露出石砌地面
scene: 工地被划成整齐的方格，工人用小铲一层层刮去表土，坑壁贴上编号纸条，坑底渐渐露出石砌地面。The excavation, the careful digging of a buried site, uncovered a wall that had lain under the field for centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 excavation 指「考古发掘的过程与工程」（第 1 个义项：有方法地把埋藏物挖出并记录）；句意为这次发掘揭开了一道在田野下埋了数百年的墙。可辨识物件：方格探坑、小铲、编号纸条、石砌地面、土堆。

pos.zh: 发掘；开挖；发掘现场或坑（可数，复数 excavations）

senses.title: The process of digging out buried material
senses.definition: the systematic removal of soil and deposits to expose remains or reach a level
senses.definitionCN: 有系统地移去土壤与堆积，以暴露遗存或到达某一层位
senses.example: The excavation uncovered a wall that had lain under the field for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发掘揭开了一道在田野下埋了数百年的墙。
senses.why: ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to hollow' gives 'hollow out'; the noun names the whole act of making a hollow.
senses.whyCN: ex-「出」加 cavare「挖空」构成「挖出空洞」；名词指整个挖空行为。

senses.title: The site or pit of a dig
senses.definition: the place, trench or pit where digging is under way
senses.definitionCN: 正在挖掘的地点、探沟或坑
senses.example: Visitors were kept back from the excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者被挡住，不能靠近发掘现场。
senses.why: the act and the place share one word because the hole is the act's visible result.
senses.whyCN: 行为与地点共用一个词，因为坑就是行为可见的结果。

senses.title: The finds produced by a dig
senses.definition: the objects and records recovered in the course of digging
senses.definitionCN: 挖掘过程中获得的物件与记录
senses.example: The excavation produced three coins and a seal.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发掘出三枚硬币和一枚印章。
senses.why: a dig is judged by what it yields, so the noun can stand for its output.
senses.whyCN: 一次发掘以其收获来评判，因此名词可代指其产出。

senses.title: Earthwork or engineering cut
senses.definition: the removal of soil for a foundation, road, tunnel or canal
senses.definitionCN: 为地基、道路、隧道或运河而移走土壤
senses.example: The excavation for the tunnel took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 隧道开挖花了两年。
senses.why: the engineering sense came first in English; archaeology later borrowed the same term.
senses.whyCN: 英语中工程义先出现，考古学后来借用了同一术语。

senses.title: The archaeological method
senses.definition: the controlled technique of digging in layers, recording context and preserving finds
senses.definitionCN: 按层位挖掘、记录背景并保存器物的受控技术
senses.example: Modern excavation records every layer before removing it.
senses.exampleCN: 现代发掘在移除每一层之前先作记录。
senses.why: once digging became a science, the word named a method rather than mere earth-moving.
senses.whyCN: 当挖掘成为科学，这个词就命名方法，而不只是搬土。

senses.title: The hole or trench left behind
senses.definition: the cavity, trench or cutting made by removal of material
senses.definitionCN: 因移走材料而形成的洞、沟或切口
senses.example: Rainwater collected in the old excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水积在旧坑里。
senses.why: the result persists after the work ends, and the noun covers that persistent shape.
senses.whyCN: 工作结束后结果仍在，名词也涵盖这一持久形状。

senses.title: Metaphor: deep investigation
senses.definition: by extension, a thorough inquiry that removes layers of concealment
senses.definitionCN: 引申指层层去除掩盖的彻底调查
senses.example: The journalist's excavation of the files took months.
senses.exampleCN: 记者对这些档案的「发掘」花了数月。
senses.why: the metaphor treats secrecy as soil: each layer removed brings evidence closer.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把秘密当作泥土：每移走一层，证据就更近一步。

senses.title: Abstraction: the uncovering of what was buried
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把埋藏之物揭开
senses.definition: any process by which something covered or forgotten is brought into view
senses.definitionCN: 任何使被覆盖或被遗忘之物显现的过程
senses.example: Excavation is memory done with tools.
senses.exampleCN: 发掘是用工具进行的记忆。
senses.why: the deepest sense is revelation by removal, whether the layers are earth, paper or silence.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是「移除以显现」，无论层是泥土、纸张还是沉默。

intro.en: Excavation comes from Latin excavare, ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to make hollow', from cavus 'hollow'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excavation 来自拉丁 excavare，由 ex-「出」与 cavare「挖空」构成，后者源于 cavus「空的」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cavus meant 'hollow, excavated'; it also gave English cavity and cave through related forms.
items.cn: cavus 意为「空的、挖空的」；它也经相关形式衍生英语 cavity 与 cave。

items.en: Cavare meant 'to make hollow, to dig out'; it turned the adjective into a verb of action.
items.cn: cavare 意为「使成空、挖出」；它把形容词变成动作动词。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus cavare produced excavare, 'to hollow out, dig out'.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 cavare 构成 excavare，意为「挖空、挖出」。

items.en: Excavatio named a hollowing out; English excavation came from this action noun.
items.cn: excavatio 指挖空；英语 excavation 来自这个行为名词。

items.en: Excavation entered English in the seventeenth century for earthworks; the archaeological sense developed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: excavation 在十七世纪进入英语，指土方工程；考古义在十九世纪发展起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and root shape): dictionaries differ on the earliest English use, and the pre-Latin root of cavus is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与词根形态）：辞书对最早的英语用例说法不一，cavus 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds digging words easily confused with excavation; group two holds neighbouring ideas of removal and discovery.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 excavation 混淆的挖掘类词；第二组是移走与发现的邻近概念。

entries.definition: To carry out excavation; the noun names the work, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行发掘；名词指工作，动词指去做。

entries.definition: A person or machine that excavates; it names the doer, not the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施开挖的人或机器；命名施动者，而非行为。

entries.definition: A hollow space, especially in a tooth or body; it shares the root but names the void, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指空洞，尤指牙体或身体中的腔；同词根，但命名空处，而非工作。

entries.definition: A long narrow ditch; it can be the product of excavation or a separate military work.
entries.definitionCN: 指狭长沟；它可以是开挖的产物，也可以是单独的军事工事。

entries.definition: To break and remove ground; it is general and informal, while excavation implies method and record.
entries.definitionCN: 指破土并移走土；日常而宽泛，而 excavation 暗示方法与记录。

entries.definition: Digging to extract ore or coal; its purpose is economic, not archaeological.
entries.definitionCN: 指为开采矿石或煤而挖；目的在经济效益，而非考古。

entries.definition: Taking stone or sand from an open pit; the scale and purpose differ from a research dig.
entries.definitionCN: 指从露天坑取石或取砂；规模与目的不同于研究性发掘。

entries.definition: Bringing a buried thing to light; it stresses the find rather than the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指使埋藏物见光；强调发现，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin pieces, the engineering-first history and the layer-by-layer method.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁成分、工程义在先的历史，以及逐层发掘的方法。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cavare 'hollow': to hollow out the ground.
normal.cn: ex-「出」+ cavare「挖空」：把地面挖空。

normal.en: The family runs excavate, excavation, excavator, cavity, cave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excavate、excavation、excavator、cavity、cave。

normal.en: Engineering came first in English; archaeology borrowed the word later.
normal.cn: 英语中工程义在先；考古学后来借用了这个词。

normal.en: A modern dig records each layer before removing it.
normal.cn: 现代发掘在移除每一层之前先记录。

normal.en: Typical partners are archaeological, rescue, site and work.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「考古的」「抢救性的」「现场」与「工程」。

abstract.en: Picture a hole that is also a notebook: every spadeful is written down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个坑同时也是一本笔记：每一铲都被记下。

abstract.en: Picture layers of paint removed from a wall until an older image appears.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的层层颜料被去掉，直到旧画显现。

abstract.en: Picture a secret buried in paper rather than soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一个秘密埋在纸里，而不是土里。

examples.en: The excavation was halted when the water table rose.
examples.cn: 当地下水位上升时，发掘被停止。

examples.en: Every excavation destroys what it does not record.
examples.cn: 每一次发掘都会毁掉它未记录的东西。

examples.en: The road excavation exposed three old foundations.
examples.cn: 道路开挖露出了三处旧地基。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ cav（洞）+ ation」——把洞挖出来 → 发掘；开挖

root: 拉丁 excavatio，来自 excavare「挖空」= ex-（出）+ cavare（使空），cavare 源于 cavus「空的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one hollow: earth is removed. The hollow becomes a process, a place, a set of finds, an engineering cut, a method, a lasting hole, a metaphor for inquiry and finally any uncovering by removal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个空洞展开：土被移走。这个空洞先成为过程，再成为地点、一组出土物、工程切口、方法、留下的坑、调查的比喻，最后成为任何「移除以显现」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stepped pit narrowing downward, tags on the walls, a stone floor at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：逐层收窄的阶梯探坑，坑壁插着标签，坑底露出石地面。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE PLACE: the hollow is both work and workplace.
branches.cn: 行为与地点：空洞既是工作，也是工作场所。

branches.en: THE YIELD AND THE HOLE: what comes out and what remains are two ends of one act.
branches.cn: 收获与坑：取出之物与留下之物是同一行为的两端。

branches.en: ENGINEERING AND METHOD: moving soil becomes a science when records matter.
branches.cn: 工程与方法：当记录变得重要，搬土就成为科学。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: secrecy is soil, and inquiry is the spade.
branches.cn: 比喻：秘密是土，调查是铲。

branches.en: REVELATION BY REMOVAL: the deepest sense covers earth, paper and silence alike.
branches.cn: 移除以显现：最深的一层同时涵盖泥土、纸张与沉默。

intro.en: Excavation is a Latin verb plus an action suffix; the root cavus also builds words for hollow spaces.
intro.cn: excavation 是拉丁动词加行为后缀；词根 cavus 也构成表示空腔的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavus and cavare give cavity, cave, excavate and excavation; ex- adds the direction outward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavus 与 cavare 衍生 cavity、cave、excavate 与 excavation；ex- 增添向外的方向。

items.example: The prefix marks removal outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出向外的移走。

items.example: The adjective describes the space made.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述被造出的空间。

items.example: The verb turns emptiness into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「空」变成动作。

items.example: The Latin verb covered both engineering and burial.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词兼指工程与埋藏。

items.example: Excavation names the process and its result.
items.exampleCN: excavation 兼指过程与结果。

items.example: They excavated the floor to the bedrock.
items.exampleCN: 他们把地面挖到基岩。

items.structure: excavate + -or (one who or that which acts)
items.example: The excavator lifted a bucket of clay.
items.exampleCN: 挖掘机提起一斗黏土。

items.example: The cavity in the tooth was filled.
items.exampleCN: 牙上的洞被补好。

items.example: The cave kept a constant temperature.
items.exampleCN: 洞穴保持恒温。

latinEntries.structure: cavus, cava, cavum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 挖掘；发掘（遗址）；挖出；挖空；揭示（隐藏的事实）
definition_en: to dig out earth or buried material, to hollow out a space, or to bring hidden facts to light
core_image: 一把铲子切入土层，土被抛向一侧，坑底露出一块刻字的石头
scene: 探方里，工作人员先用铲子切开草皮，再把土一筐筐运到筛网旁，坑底露出一块刻字石头。They excavate the trench by hand, removing the soil layer by layer, so that no small find is lost.
sceneCN: 这里 excavate 指「按层挖开遗址」（第 1 个义项：以手工方式挖掘并保留细节）；句意为他们手工挖掘这条探沟，以免任何细小发现被漏掉。可辨识物件：铲子、草皮、土筐、筛网、刻字石头。

pos.zh: 挖掘；发掘；挖出（过去式 excavated，过去分词 excavated，现在分词 excavating）
进行挖掘；（场地等）容易被挖开

senses.title: To dig out earth
senses.definition: to remove soil or rock in order to make a hole, cutting or level
senses.definitionCN: 为形成洞、切口或平面而移走土或岩石
senses.example: They excavate the trench by hand so that no small find is lost.
senses.exampleCN: 他们手工挖掘这条探沟，以免任何细小发现被漏掉。
senses.why: ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to hollow' means the verb is literally 'to hollow out'.
senses.whyCN: ex-「出」加 cavare「挖空」，因此这个动词字面就是「挖空」。

senses.title: To dig an archaeological site
senses.definition: to remove deposits layer by layer in order to expose and record remains
senses.definitionCN: 逐层移去堆积，以暴露并记录遗存
senses.example: Students excavate the floor in squares of one metre.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们按一米方格发掘地面。
senses.why: the verb followed the noun into archaeology and now implies method, not only muscle.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词随名词进入考古学，如今暗示方法，而不只是力气。

senses.title: To dig out an object
senses.definition: to free a buried object by removing the material around it
senses.definitionCN: 通过移走周围材料使埋藏物脱出
senses.example: They excavated the jar without breaking its rim.
senses.exampleCN: 他们挖出陶罐，没有弄破罐口。
senses.why: the object is the goal, and the verb can take it as a direct object.
senses.whyCN: 物件是目标，动词可以把它作直接宾语。

senses.title: To hollow out a space
senses.definition: to form a cavity, tunnel or channel inside a mass
senses.definitionCN: 在实体内部形成腔、隧道或通道
senses.example: Workers excavated a passage through the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 工人穿过山体开凿了一条通道。
senses.why: here the verb creates empty space rather than exposing something.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词创造空处，而不是暴露某物。

senses.title: To cut in engineering or geology
senses.definition: to remove material for a foundation, road, canal or mine
senses.definitionCN: 为地基、道路、运河或矿井移走材料
senses.example: The company excavated the slope for the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为新路开挖山坡。
senses.why: the engineering sense is the oldest English use and remains the commonest outside archaeology.
senses.whyCN: 工程义是英语中最早的用法，在考古之外仍最常见。

senses.title: To uncover hidden facts
senses.definition: by extension, to search through records or evidence until what was concealed appears
senses.definitionCN: 引申指翻查记录或证据，直到被掩盖之物显现
senses.example: The reporter excavated the old correspondence.
senses.exampleCN: 记者翻查旧通信，把内情挖了出来。
senses.why: the metaphor treats archives as strata, and the verb keeps its 'remove to reveal' shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把档案当作地层，动词保留「移走以显现」的形状。

senses.title: The dental sense
senses.definition: to hollow out decayed tissue from a tooth before filling it
senses.definitionCN: 补牙前把牙上的腐坏组织挖除
senses.example: The dentist excavated the cavity before the filling.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在填补之前挖除了龋洞。
senses.why: dentistry borrowed the literal sense: a small cavity is hollowed with a small tool.
senses.whyCN: 牙科借用字面义：用小工具把小小的腔挖空。

senses.title: Abstraction: to peel away layers
senses.definition: any process of removing layer after layer until a hidden structure is seen
senses.definitionCN: 层层移除直到看见隐藏结构的任何过程
senses.example: To understand the custom, she excavated its assumptions.
senses.exampleCN: 为了理解这一习俗，她层层挖出它的预设。
senses.why: the deepest sense needs no soil: any covering can be excavated if it can be removed in layers.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层不需要泥土：任何能被逐层移除的覆盖物都可被「发掘」。

intro.en: Excavate is recorded in English in the late sixteenth century; it may come from the Latin participle excavatus or from the noun excavation, and dictionaries differ. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excavate 在十六世纪晚期见于英语；它可能来自拉丁过去分词 excavatus，也可能由名词 excavation 派生，辞书说法不一。年代均为约数。

items.en: The past participle excavatus meant 'hollowed out', and it is one plausible source of the English verb.
items.cn: 过去分词 excavatus 意为「被挖空的」，是英语动词的可能来源之一。

items.en: English excavate appears in the late sixteenth century; whether it was taken from the Latin participle or formed from excavation is not settled, so both paths are listed rather than one ruling.
items.cn: 英语 excavate 出现于十六世纪晚期；它是取自拉丁过去分词，还是由 excavation 派生，尚无定论，因此两条路径并列，不作单一判定。

items.en: The first English uses concerned foundations, canals and mines, where the verb meant simply to remove ground.
items.cn: 最早的英语用法涉及地基、运河与矿井，动词只表示移走土方。

items.en: Systematic archaeology in the nineteenth century gave the verb its layer-by-layer, record-keeping sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪系统考古学赋予这个动词逐层、留记录的义项。

items.en: Dentistry applied the verb to the small-scale hollowing of a decayed tooth, preserving the literal image.
items.cn: 牙科把这个动词用于牙体腐坏处的小规模挖除，保留了字面意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and noun-verb path): dictionaries differ on the earliest use, and the relation between the noun and the verb is reconstructed from citation patterns rather than documented in a single statement.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与名动关系）：辞书对最早的用例说法不一，名词与动词之间的关系是依书证模式重构的，并没有单一文献直接说明。

note.en: Group one holds verbs of digging easily confused with excavate; group two holds verbs of revealing.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 excavate 混淆的挖掘动词；第二组是揭示类动词。

entries.definition: To break and remove ground; it lacks the methodical, recorded sense that excavate carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指破土移土；缺少 excavate 所含的有方法、留记录的意味。

entries.definition: To dig a hole or tunnel, especially as an animal does; the scale is small and the agent often non-human.
entries.definitionCN: 指挖洞或掘隧道，尤指动物所为；规模小，施动者常非人。

entries.definition: To make something empty inside; it shares the cavus image but says nothing about exposing remains.
entries.definitionCN: 指使内部变空；共享 cavus 意象，但不涉及暴露遗存。

entries.definition: To take up mud or objects from a river or seabed; the medium is water, not soil.
entries.definitionCN: 指从河底或海床取泥或取物；介质是水，而非土。

entries.definition: To discover something buried or hidden; it stresses the find rather than the digging method.
entries.definitionCN: 指发现埋藏或隐藏之物；强调发现，而非挖掘方法。

entries.definition: To remove a body from the ground; it is a legal and forensic term, narrower than excavate.
entries.definitionCN: 指从地下取出遗体；是法律与法医术语，比 excavate 窄。

entries.definition: To dig for ore or coal; the aim is extraction, not research.
entries.definitionCN: 指为矿石或煤而挖；目的在开采，而非研究。

entries.definition: To make a long narrow cut in the ground, often for defence or drainage.
entries.definitionCN: 指在地面挖狭长沟，常用于防御或排水。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin pieces, the back-formation and the four settings of the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁成分、逆构过程，以及这个动词的四种场景。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cavare 'hollow': to hollow out.
normal.cn: ex-「出」+ cavare「挖空」：把东西挖空。

normal.en: The verb is a back-formation from excavation, not a direct Latin loan at first.
normal.cn: 这个动词由 excavation 逆构而来，最初不是直接借自拉丁。

normal.en: The family runs excavate, excavation, excavator, cavity, cave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excavate、excavation、excavator、cavity、cave。

normal.en: Four settings: foundations, archaeology, tunnels and teeth.
normal.cn: 四种场景：地基、考古、隧道与牙齿。

normal.en: Typical partners are site, trench, by hand, foundations.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「遗址」「沟」「手工」与「地基」。

abstract.en: Picture a spade that turns over not soil but assumptions.
abstract.cn: 想象一把铲子翻起的不是土，而是预设。

abstract.en: Picture a floor dug in squares so that nothing is missed.
abstract.cn: 想象地面被划成方格挖掘，以免遗漏。

abstract.en: Picture a hole made on purpose so that something else can be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象故意挖出的一个洞，为的是看见别的东西。

examples.en: Archaeologists excavate slowly when the soil is wet.
examples.cn: 土壤潮湿时，考古学家会缓慢发掘。

examples.en: The crew excavated the old cellar before building the tower.
examples.cn: 在建塔之前，施工队挖开了旧地窖。

examples.en: The dentist excavated the decay and filled the tooth.
examples.cn: 牙医挖除腐坏部分并补好了牙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ cav（洞）+ ate（做）」——把洞挖出来 → 挖掘；发掘

root: 英语 excavate 见于十六世纪晚期，可能来自拉丁过去分词 excavatus，也可能由 excavation 派生，辞书说法不一；excavation 来自拉丁 excavare「挖空」= ex-（出）+ cavare（使空），cavare 源于 cavus「空的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one spade: material is removed. The act becomes plain digging, then archaeological method, then freeing an object, hollowing a passage, engineering, uncovering facts, dental work and finally the peeling of any layers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一把铲子展开：材料被移走。这个动作先成为普通挖掘，再成为考古方法、取出物件、挖通通道、工程开挖、揭示事实、牙科操作，最后成为任何层层剥离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spade cutting into soil, earth thrown to one side, a carved stone appearing at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：铲子切入土中，土被抛向一侧，坑底露出一块刻字石头。

branches.en: THE PLAIN CUT: foundations and roads need only removal.
branches.cn: 普通切口：地基与道路只需要移走。

branches.en: METHOD AND OBJECT: careful layers free a find without breaking it.
branches.cn: 方法与物件：细致的分层能在不破坏的情况下取出发现。

branches.en: THE SMALL CAVITY: tunnels and teeth are hollowed by the same image.
branches.cn: 小空腔：隧道与牙齿用同一意象挖空。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: archives become strata and facts become finds.
branches.cn: 比喻：档案成为地层，事实成为出土物。

branches.en: PEELING LAYERS: the deepest sense needs no earth at all.
branches.cn: 剥离层：最深的一层根本不需要泥土。

intro.en: Excavate is a verb made of a Latin prefix and root, with a noun family that keeps the hollow image.
intro.cn: excavate 是由拉丁前缀与词根构成的动词，其名词词族保留「空」的意象。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavus and cavare give cavity, cave, excavate and excavation; ex- supplies the outward direction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavus 与 cavare 衍生 cavity、cave、excavate 与 excavation；ex- 提供向外方向。

items.example: The prefix makes the hollowing an outward removal.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使挖空成为向外的移走。

items.example: The root supplies the shape of the result.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供结果的形状。

items.example: The verb supplies the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词提供动作。

items.example: Latin used it for both earth and buried things.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用它兼指泥土与埋藏物。

items.meaning: to remove material to expose or hollow
items.meaningCN: 移走材料以暴露或挖空
items.example: They excavated the pit in squares.
items.exampleCN: 他们把坑划成方格挖掘。

items.meaning: the act or result of digging
items.example: The excavation took three seasons.
items.exampleCN: 这次发掘用了三个季度。

items.meaning: one who or that which digs
items.example: The excavator reached the clay layer.
items.exampleCN: 挖掘机挖到黏土层。

items.example: The cavity was cleaned before filling.
items.exampleCN: 补牙前先清理了龋洞。

items.example: The cave entrance faced north.
items.exampleCN: 洞穴入口朝北。

definition_zh: 挖掘机；挖掘者；考古发掘人员；牙科挖除器械
definition_en: a machine or person that digs out earth or buried material, or a dental instrument for hollowing a cavity
core_image: 一台履带机器把斗臂伸进土坑，铲斗落下，旁边一名工人举着标杆示意深度
scene: 雨后的工地上，一台履带机器把斗臂伸进坑里，铲斗每次落下都带起湿土，测量员在旁举着标杆。The excavator, a machine with a steel bucket, cut a trench beside the road before the pipes arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 excavator 指「用于开挖土方的机械」（第 1 个义项：以铲斗挖掘的工程机械）；句意为这台挖掘机在管道运到之前就在路边挖好了一条沟。可辨识物件：履带、斗臂、铲斗、湿土、测量标杆。

pos.zh: 挖掘机；挖掘者；牙科挖器（可数，复数 excavators）

senses.title: A digging machine
senses.definition: a powered machine with a bucket or scoop used to move earth and rock
senses.definitionCN: 带铲斗或勺斗、用于移动土石的动力机械
senses.example: The excavator cut a trench beside the road before the pipes arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 这台挖掘机在管道运到之前就在路边挖好了一条沟。
senses.why: excavate plus -or names the agent; when the agent is a machine, the suffix covers it as naturally as a person.
senses.whyCN: excavate 加 -or 命名施动者；当施动者是机器时，这个后缀同样自然涵盖它。

senses.title: The operator of such a machine
senses.definition: a person trained to run an excavating machine
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、操作挖掘机械的人
senses.example: The excavator signalled the truck to move forward.
senses.exampleCN: 挖掘机操作员示意卡车向前移动。
senses.why: English often uses the machine name for the person who runs it, by metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用机器名称指操作它的人，这是转喻。

senses.title: An archaeological digger
senses.definition: a person who excavates a site, especially in a professional team
senses.definitionCN: 发掘遗址的人，尤指专业团队中的成员
senses.example: The excavator kept a notebook beside the trench.
senses.exampleCN: 这位发掘者在探沟旁放着一本笔记。
senses.why: the older personal sense survives in archaeology, where the tool is often small and the hand is human.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的人物义在考古学中保留下来，因为那里的工具常很小，施动的是人手。

senses.title: A type of machine
senses.definition: a class such as tracked, wheeled, backhoe or bucket-wheel excavator
senses.definitionCN: 履带式、轮式、反铲式或斗轮式等类别
senses.example: A bucket-wheel excavator can move a trainload of earth in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 一台斗轮式挖掘机一小时能搬走一列车那么重的土。
senses.why: machines are classified by undercarriage and bucket, and the noun takes those modifiers.
senses.whyCN: 机械按底盘与铲斗分类，这个名词可带这些修饰语。

senses.title: The plant or contractor in engineering
senses.titleCN: 工程中的机械或承包方
senses.definition: the machine fleet or contractor responsible for excavation on a project
senses.definitionCN: 项目中负责开挖的机械队或承包方
senses.example: The excavator was booked for the whole week.
senses.exampleCN: 挖掘机被订了整整一周。
senses.why: in project speech, the machine stands for the service it performs.
senses.whyCN: 在项目口语中，机器代指它提供的服务。

senses.title: A dental excavator
senses.definition: a small hand instrument used to remove decayed tissue from a tooth
senses.definitionCN: 用于挖除牙体腐坏组织的小型手用器械
senses.example: The dentist chose a small excavator for the edge of the cavity.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医选了一把小挖器处理龋洞边缘。
senses.why: dentistry keeps the literal sense at a tiny scale: a hand tool that hollows.
senses.whyCN: 牙科在极小尺度保留字面义：一把挖空的手用工具。

senses.title: Metaphor: a person who digs out truth
senses.definition: by extension, someone who searches persistently through records or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 引申指持续翻查记录或证据的人
senses.example: The archivist was the excavator of the vanished company.
senses.exampleCN: 这位档案员是那家消失公司的「挖掘者」。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the agent role: someone operates the tool that removes layers.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留施动角色：有人操作移除层层的工具。

senses.title: Abstraction: a tool that reveals what is buried
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：使埋藏之物显现的工具
senses.definition: any instrument or method by which covered material is brought into view
senses.definitionCN: 任何使被覆盖材料显现的工具或方法
senses.example: A good question is an excavator for a silent room.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好问题是对沉默房间的「挖掘机」。
senses.why: the deepest sense separates the tool from its material: whatever removes cover can be called an excavator.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层把工具与材料分开：任何移除覆盖之物都可称为挖掘器。

intro.en: Excavator is excavate plus the Latin agent suffix -or. The machine sense is nineteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excavator 是 excavate 加拉丁施动后缀 -or；机器义出现在十九世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Excavare meant 'to hollow out, dig out', from ex- 'out' and cavare 'to make hollow'.
items.cn: excavare 意为「挖空、挖出」，来自 ex-「出」与 cavare「使空」。

items.en: Latin -or named the person who performs an action; English keeps it in agent nouns such as actor and creator.
items.cn: 拉丁 -or 命名实施动作的人；英语在 actor、creator 等施动名词中保留它。

items.en: A Latin agent noun excavator exists mainly as a formed pattern rather than a common classical word, so English excavator is best treated as an English formation on Latin pieces.
items.cn: 拉丁施动名词 excavator 主要作为一种构词模式存在，并非古典时期的常用词，因此英语 excavator 宜视为用拉丁成分构成的英语词。

items.en: Steam shovels and dredgers in the nineteenth century gave the agent noun a mechanical referent, and the machine sense now dominates.
items.cn: 十九世纪的蒸汽铲与挖泥船使这个施动名词获得机械所指，机器义如今占主导。

items.en: The older personal sense survives for archaeologists, and dentistry uses the same word for a small hand tool.
items.cn: 较古老的人物义在考古学家身上保留，牙科则用同一个词指小型手用工具。

items.en: Source uncertain (first machine use and Latin status): the exact date of the machine sense is not fixed, and the classical standing of Latin excavator is doubtful.
items.cn: 来源不确定（机器义首见与拉丁语地位）：机器义的确切年代无定论，拉丁 excavator 在古典时期的地位可疑。

note.en: Group one holds digger words easily confused with excavator; group two holds neighbouring machines and roles.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 excavator 混淆的挖掘类词；第二组是邻近的机械与角色。

entries.definition: The process or hole of digging; excavator names the machine or person that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 指挖掘过程或坑；excavator 指做这件事的机器或人。

entries.definition: To dig out; the agent noun adds the doer to the action.
entries.definitionCN: 指挖出；施动名词在动作之外加上施动者。

entries.definition: A person or machine that digs; it is less technical and does not specify a bucket arm.
entries.definitionCN: 指挖掘的人或机器；较少技术性，不特指斗臂机械。

entries.definition: A machine that removes mud from the seabed or a river; the medium differs from dry excavation.
entries.definitionCN: 指从海床或河底取泥的机械；介质不同于干地开挖。

entries.definition: An excavating arm mounted on a tractor, digging toward itself; it is a kind of excavator.
entries.definitionCN: 指装在拖拉机上的反铲臂，向自身方向挖；是挖掘机的一种。

entries.definition: A machine with a blade that pushes soil; it moves material forward rather than lifting it.
entries.definitionCN: 指用推土铲推土的机械；把材料向前推，而非铲起。

entries.definition: Any large machine for moving soil; excavator is one member of that class.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何搬运土方的大型机械；挖掘机是其中一员。

entries.definition: Anyone who runs a machine; it does not specify the machine as excavator does.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作机器的人，泛称；不像 excavator 那样标明机器种类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the verb plus -or, the machine family and the small dental tool.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：动词加 -or、机械词族，以及那把小型牙科器械。

normal.en: excavate + -or: the one that digs.
normal.cn: excavate + -or：挖掘的那一个。

normal.en: -or is the Latin agent ending also seen in actor, creator and inspector.
normal.cn: -or 是拉丁施动词尾，也见于 actor、creator 与 inspector。

normal.en: The family runs excavate, excavation, excavator, cavity, cave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excavate、excavation、excavator、cavity、cave。

normal.en: The machine sense is nineteenth-century, when steam shovels replaced hand gangs.
normal.cn: 机器义出现在十九世纪，当时蒸汽铲取代了人工队。

normal.en: Dentistry keeps a tiny excavator for a tiny hollow.
normal.cn: 牙科保留一把小挖器，用于小小的空腔。

abstract.en: Picture a steel arm that reaches into the ground like a hand into a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一条钢臂伸进地里，像手伸进抽屉。

abstract.en: Picture a bucket that brings up one layer at a time and never takes two at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个铲斗一次只带起一层，从不同时取两层。

abstract.en: Picture a tool that is judged by what it uncovers, not by what it moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一件工具，评价它的是它揭开了什么，而不是它搬走了什么。

examples.en: The excavator was too heavy for the narrow street.
examples.cn: 这台挖掘机太重，进不了这条窄街。

examples.en: An excavator operator must watch for buried cables.
examples.cn: 挖掘机操作员必须留意地下电缆。

examples.en: The dental excavator removed the softened dentine.
examples.cn: 牙科挖器去除了软化的牙本质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「excavate（挖）+ or（东西/人）」——负责挖的那台机器或那个人 → 挖掘机；发掘者

root: excavate 加拉丁施动后缀 -or；excavate 由 excavation 逆构，源自拉丁 excavare「挖空」= ex-（出）+ cavare（使空）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one agent: the thing or person that digs. The agent becomes a machine, its operator, an archaeological digger, a machine type, a hired plant, a dental tool, a metaphor for an investigator and finally any instrument that reveals what is buried.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个施动者展开：挖的那台东西或那个人。这个施动者先成为机器，再成为操作员、考古发掘者、机械类型、租用的机械、牙科工具、调查者的比喻，最后成为任何使埋藏物显现的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tracked machine reaching its boom into a pit, the bucket biting wet soil, a surveyor's rod beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：履带机器把斗臂伸进坑里，铲斗咬住湿土，旁边立着测量标杆。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND ITS KINDS: one agent, many undercarriages and buckets.
branches.cn: 机器及其种类：同一个施动者，多种底盘与铲斗。

branches.en: THE HUMAN HAND: the operator and the archaeological digger share the name.
branches.cn: 人手：操作员与考古发掘者共用这个名称。

branches.en: THE SERVICE AND THE SMALL TOOL: a hired plant and a dental instrument both act on material.
branches.cn: 服务与小工具：租用的机械与牙科器械都作用于材料。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: an investigator becomes the one who removes layers.
branches.cn: 比喻：调查者成为移除层层的人。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: the deepest sense is any tool that brings buried things into view.
branches.cn: 工具：最深的一层是任何使埋藏物显现的器具。

intro.en: Excavator is a verb plus the Latin agent suffix -or, so it reads as 'the one that digs'.
intro.cn: excavator 是动词加拉丁施动后缀 -or，因此可读作「挖掘的那一个」。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavare and excavare give excavate and excavation; the agent ending -or also builds actor, creator and inspector.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavare 与 excavare 衍生 excavate 与 excavation；施动词尾 -or 也构成 actor、creator 与 inspector。

items.example: The crew excavate the site in summer.
items.exampleCN: 施工队在夏天开挖场地。

items.meaning: one who or that which acts
items.example: The suffix turns an action into an agent.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成施动者。

items.example: The excavator lifted the bucket.
items.exampleCN: 挖掘机提起铲斗。

items.example: The excavation lasted all summer.
items.exampleCN: 发掘持续了整个夏天。

items.example: The root describes the space made.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描述造出的空间。

items.example: The verb supplies the action behind the agent.
items.exampleCN: 这个词提供施动背后的动作。

items.example: The cavity was small but deep.
items.exampleCN: 这个洞小而深。

items.meaning: an excavating arm on a tractor
items.example: The backhoe dug close to the wall.
items.exampleCN: 反铲贴着墙挖。

items.meaning: a machine that removes mud from water
items.example: The dredger cleared the channel.
items.exampleCN: 挖泥船清理了航道。
